title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration-approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL's efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS. A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs. Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.

title: Epstein-Barr Virus Serologic Profiles in Multiple Sclerosis and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease.
abstract: Although the link between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and multiple sclerosis (MS) is well established, geographic variation in EBV epidemiology warrants region-specific data from Asian populations. Beyond MS, the role of EBV in myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) remains far less studied. This study aimed to compare EBV serostatus and antibody titers in patients with MS, MOGAD, and controls in a Korean cohort. We analyzed MS (n = 130), MOGAD (n = 125), and untreated tumor controls without known EBV association (n = 132). MS and controls were frequency-matched to MOGAD by age at sampling. Serum Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) IgG, viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgG, VCA IgM, and early antigen (EA) IgG were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassays (LIAISON, DiaSorin). EBV seropositivity was defined as EBNA1 IgG or VCA IgG positivity, and serologic findings suggestive of possible recent infection/reactivation were defined as positivity for VCA IgM or EA IgG. EBV seropositivity was nearly universal in MS, MOGAD, and controls (98.5%, 98.4%, and 99.2%, In this Korean cohort, MS showed stronger EBNA1 responses than MOGAD and controls, extending prior evidence on the relevance of EBNA1 in MS to an Asian population. The absence of a similar pattern in MOGAD suggests that the contribution of EBV may differ between the 2 diseases.

title: Genetic Variation Underlying CSF Natural Killer T-Cell Frequency in Inflammatory CNS Diseases: A Genome-Wide Association Study.
abstract: Natural killer T (NKT) cells bridge innate and adaptive immunity and are implicated in immune regulation in autoimmune diseases. In multiple sclerosis (MS), reduced CSF frequencies of NKT cells have been reported, but their role in disease pathogenesis remains unclear. Here, we investigated the genetic architecture underlying CSF NKT cell frequency variability in individuals with MS and other CNS diseases. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of CSF NKT cell frequencies in 456 individuals with MS, with replication in an independent cohort of 90 individuals with MS or other inflammatory CNS diseases. Functional follow-up assessed effects of the lead variant on integrin subunit beta 5 ( We identified and replicated a novel genome-wide significant association of rs6783734*C (joint Our findings implicate ITGB5 as a potentially context-dependent modulator of immune cell dynamics in inflammatory CNS disease, linking genetic variation to NKT cell frequencies within the CNS compartment. Given the central role of integrins in immune cell trafficking and the therapeutic success of integrin-targeting agents in MS, these results highlight integrin-mediated pathways as determinants of CNS immune responses. Although the observed association of higher CSF NKT cell frequencies with greater disease severity suggests that integrating genetic factors and immune phenotypes may ultimately prove useful for patient stratification, this finding requires confirmation in larger studies.

title: Cuprizone-Induced Demyelination and Remyelination Models of Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is marked by central nervous system inflammation, demyelination, and neuronal injury, leading to cumulative neurological deficits. Despite reducing relapse rates, current therapies have limited impact on slowing disability accumulation in progressive forms of MS and do not directly promote remyelination. The cuprizone model is one of the most widely used demyelination models for studying oligodendrocyte death, myelin loss, and spontaneous remyelination. Remyelination is often impaired in MS lesions, and because cuprizone-induced demyelination often recovers quickly, it does not model inflammation-mediated inhibition of remyelination. Therefore, cuprizone can be combined with adoptive transfer of activated myelin-specific CD4⁺ T cells at the onset of spontaneous repair, and this combination model is referred to as the adoptive transfer-cuprizone (ATCup) paradigm, which recapitulates the immune-mediated suppression of remyelination seen in MS. This chapter provides detailed protocols for the cuprizone and ATCup paradigms, including immune cell generation and transfer, tissue processing, and quantitative histology. These models enable mechanistic studies of demyelination and repair and facilitate testing of drugs that protect oligodendrocytes and promote remyelination.

title: Myelinating Co-Cultures with CNS-Derived Axons and Analysis of Myelin Formation with Live Imaging.
abstract: Myelin is a lipid-rich insulating membrane that enables rapid and precise signal conduction along nerve fibers. Loss or damage of myelin is a hallmark of demyelinating diseases such as multiple sclerosis, underscoring the need for experimental systems that reveal how myelin is formed and maintained. Here we describe a neuron-oligodendrocyte co-culture method amenable to live-cell imaging of CNS myelination, with particular emphasis on generating a highly purified axonal substrate. Retinal ganglion cells (RGCs; the excitatory neurons whose highly myelinated axons project through the optic nerve to the brain) are isolated from rat retinas and purified by immunopanning to deplete other retinal cell types (e.g., glia and other types of neurons), yielding a highly pure population of CNS neurons suitable for myelination assays. Purified RGCs are maintained in culture to allow robust axonal outgrowth, after which oligodendrocyte lineage cells are added (typically 14-21 days after neuronal plating). Within ~6 days of co-culture, oligodendrocyte-axon interactions and axonal ensheathment are readily detectable and can be followed longitudinally by time-lapse microscopy. The system is compatible with fluorescent reporters and indicators, enabling correlation of myelin sheath initiation and growth with subcellular events such as calcium dynamics and regulated exocytosis. Overall, this method provides a scalable, experimentally tractable platform for mechanistic perturbations and comparative studies of CNS myelination.

title: Gyroscopic Radiosurgery for Trigeminal Neuralgia: Results of a Retrospective Series of >50 Patients.
abstract: Stereotactic radiosurgery (SRS) is an established treatment option for medically refractory trigeminal neuralgia (TN). However, clinical evidence regarding dedicated gyroscopic radiosurgery systems remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy, latency of response, safety, retreatment rate, and potential clinical and dosimetric predictors of outcome following ZAP-X gyroscopic radiosurgery for TN. A consecutive series of patients with pharmacologically refractory TN treated with ZAP-X gyroscopic radiosurgery between February 2023 and September 2025 was analyzed. Treatment consisted of a single isocenter targeting approximately 5 mm of the cisternal-retrogasserian trigeminal nerve, with a maximum dose of 90 Gy and a V70 Gy coverage objective ≥ 50%, using 4 or 5 mm collimators. Pain outcome was assessed using the Barrow Neurological Institute Pain Intensity Scale (BNI), and sensory toxicity was evaluated using the BNI Facial Numbness Scale. Clinical and treatment-related predictors of failure and retreatment were explored using binary logistic regression. Following radiosurgery, 87.5% of patients achieved satisfactory pain control (BNI I-IIIb; 95% CI, 78.8-96.2%), with a significant overall improvement in BNI score compared with baseline ( Gyroscopic radiosurgery with ZAP-X provides high rates of pain control, rapid clinical response, and a favorable safety profile in patients with refractory TN. Greater baseline pain severity appears to be associated with poorer treatment response. These findings support ZAP-X as an effective frameless radiosurgical alternative for TN, although larger prospective studies are required to identify robust clinical, dosimetric, and radiobiological predictors of long-term outcome.

title: Siponimod Induces Peripheral T Cell Redistribution Without Affecting Glial Cells or Behavior in Naïve Mice.
Changes in Functional Performance During and After a Supervised Exercise Programme in People with Multiple Sclerosis: A Secondary Uncontrolled Longitudinal Study.
abstract: Exercise is clinically relevant for people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS), but participation in structured programmes is often intermittent. This exploratory study described changes in functional and exercise-related outcomes during and after a supervised exercise programme. This secondary uncontrolled longitudinal analysis included 20 adults with MS who had three consecutive assessments: before (T1) and after (T2) a 12-week programme comprising two weekly 60-min supervised sessions, and after an approximately three-month period without supervised training. Outcomes included functional performance, gait parameters, fatigue and exercise-testing outcomes. Linear mixed-effects models were used as the main longitudinal analysis, with paired Wilcoxon tests as complementary comparisons. The median 2-Minute Walk Test distance increased from 121 m at baseline to 126 m after the programme and was 125 m at follow-up. The corresponding mixed-model estimate for T2 versus T1 was 5.00 m (95% CI: -0.29 to 10.29; Modest within-group changes were observed in selected walking and exercise-test-derived outcomes, but the findings were not consistently supported across statistical approaches. Given the small sample and absence of a control group, the results should be considered exploratory and cannot establish programme effectiveness or programme-related preservation of function.

title: Pediatric-Onset Multiple Sclerosis in the Gulf: A Scoping Review of the Current Evidence Base and Research Gaps.
Drug Delivery Vehicle-Teriflunomide Interactions Affect Treatment and Fluorine Magnetic Resonance in an Animal Model of Multiple Sclerosis.
Epidural Spinal Cord Stimulation for Spasticity: A Systematic Review.
journal: Neuromodulation : journal of the International Neuromodulation Society
abstract: Hypertonia resulting from central nervous system damage impairs mobility, induces pain, and diminishes quality of life, with conventional therapies having limited efficacy. This systematic review assesses the efficacy, safety, and quantitative outcomes of epidural spinal cord stimulation (eSCS) for refractory spasticity in adults, with an emphasis on prospective interventional studies that include objective measures. Following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (2020) guidelines, PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 2025 for prospective interventional studies and studies with prospective data collection elements (randomized controlled trials, nonrandomized trials, cohorts, and case series, n ≥ 5), involving adults (≥18 years) with spasticity of any etiology that was treated with eSCS. Records (n = 2872 after duplicates were removed) were screened independently by two reviewers; nine studies (total n = 247 patients, with 176 receiving eSCS) met the inclusion criteria. Data extraction focused on spasticity reduction (eg, Modified Ashworth Scale [MAS]), functional outcomes, safety, and adverse events. Due to study heterogeneity, a descriptive synthesis was performed. Included studies (1980-2024) predominantly involved spinal cord injury (SCI; 69%), with smaller cohorts for traumatic brain injury, stroke, and multiple sclerosis. eSCS electrode placement ranged from cervical (C3-C7) to thoracic (Th10-L1) and upper lumbar levels. Mean age was 35.6 years, and median follow-up was 12 months (range, 0.25-24 months). MAS reductions were consistent (pooled mean decrease of approximately 1.77 points; SCI subgroup mean -2.41 points from 3.65 to 1.24). Spasticity improved in most patients (reported response rates ranging from 62% to approximately 80%), with functional gains (eg, ambulation, activities of daily living, and independence) demonstrated in approximately 35% to 75% of patients. Adverse events were infrequent (<10%), mainly including hardware migration or transient autonomic dysreflexia; no deaths or irreversible deficits were reported. Prospective evidence indicates eSCS may effectively reduce spasticity, particularly in chronic SCI, with meaningful functional benefits and favorable safety. Heterogeneity in study design, stimulation and implantation parameters, outcome measures, and follow-up timing, along with small sample sizes, limits generalizability. Therefore, larger, multicenter trials with standardized reporting are needed to optimize paradigms and to define the mechanistic role in spasticity management. We suggest a minimum data set toward homogenizing future dissemination of knowledge.

title: Ocrelizumab-Induced Leukocyte Subpopulations Dynamics in Multiple Sclerosis.

Cognitive resilience and improvements in health-related quality of life over 4 years in people with relapsing multiple sclerosis treated with cladribine tablets: Results from the CLARIFY-MS Extension study.
abstract: The initial 2-year phase 4 CLARIFY-MS Parent study demonstrated improvements in health-related quality of life (HRQoL) and preserved cognitive function in cladribine tablets (CladT)-treated people with highly active relapsing multiple sclerosis (RMS). To report 4-year data on cognitive function, HRQoL, other efficacy and safety outcomes from CLARIFY-MS Extension. No additional CladT treatment was protocolled during Extension (as per approved EU label). The primary endpoint was the proportion of participants with no or minimal decline in cognitive function at Month (M) 48 after initial dose versus Parent study baseline. HRQoL, and other efficacy and safety outcomes of CladT were also assessed. Overall, 68.6% of the participants (n = 192/280) showed no or minimal decline in cognitive function at M48 versus Parent study baseline. Significant improvements in Multiple Sclerosis Quality of Life-54 scores were observed over 48 months. The beneficial effect of CladT on relapses, radiological activity and disability progression observed in the Parent study were sustained during Extension. No unexpected safety signals were detected. CLARIFY-MS Extension demonstrated sustained benefits of CladT on cognitive function and HRQoL in people with highly active RMS for ≤4 years after the initial dose. The 4-year follow-up of the BICAMS battery indicated resilience across different aspects of cognition with CladT. The durable and multidimensional effects of CladT on key efficacy outcomes observed during the 2-year treatment-period of the Parent study were confirmed over the treatment-free Years 3-4 of Extension. The existing safety profile of CladT was confirmed over 4 years. CLARIFY-MS Extension study: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04776213; clinicaltrials.gov Identifier: NCT04776213.

title: Multiple Sclerosis in Patients Over 50: Immunosenescence, Comorbidities, and the Role of Cladribine Tablets.
abstract: The treatment of multiple sclerosis (MS) in older patients is complicated by the confluence of frailty, immunosenescence, and comorbidities. With advancing age, the immune system undergoes significant changes that progressively limit its ability to mount effective responses, with a reduction of naïve lymphocytes and the accumulation of senescent T and B cells. Additionally, elderly individuals with MS tend to have a higher burden of comorbidities, which can further complicate therapeutic decision-making. In the elderly MS population, the use of aggressive immunosuppressive strategies is associated with an increased risk of infections and reduced vaccine responsiveness, and may therefore pose additional risks as compared to the younger population. This narrative review explores how immunosenescence and comorbidities need to be taken into account when choosing the most appropriate treatment. Particular attention is given to immune reconstitution therapies (IRTs), with a focus on cladribine tablets (CladT), as a possible treatment strategy in this population. A targeted literature search was conducted in PubMed/MEDLINE to identify relevant studies published up to October 2025, using combinations of terms covering multiple sclerosis, aging, older adults, immunosenescence, frailty, comorbidities, disease-modifying therapies, and cladribine. The evidence was synthesized narratively, with particular attention to the level of evidence and its applicability to older or frail patients. CladT may represent one potential therapeutic option in selected patients, as the drug is characterized by transient immune suppression followed by immune recovery. This mechanism may enable disease control while limiting continuous exposure to treatment. Clinical trials and real-world data suggest that CladT has a generally manageable safety profile and may be effective in reducing relapse rates and disability progression across age groups, although evidence in older and frail populations remains limited. In older patients, therapeutic decisions should balance treatment efficacy against the heightened risks associated with immunosenescence, comorbidities, and frailty, rather than relying on chronological age alone. Within this framework, CladT - owing to its intermittent dosing and reduced continuous immunosuppression - may be relevant in selected patients, although direct evidence in older and frail populations remains limited. An individualized approach to MS treatment in older patients is required, integrating considerations related to immunosenescence, comorbidities, and frailty. In this context, CladT may be considered among the available therapeutic options in selected patients, although further evidence in older populations is needed.

title: The Prevalence of Schizophrenia and Bipolar Disorder in Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Schizophrenia (SCZ) and bipolar disorder (BD) have been investigated in people with multiple sclerosis, with findings varying in prevalence. Our aim was to determine the global pervasiveness of SCZ and BD in people with MS. Our study followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines and was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO). Searches were performed in PubMed, Google Scholar, Europe PubMed Central, and Web of Science from their inception through April 2025. R statistical software was used for sensitivity analysis, subgroup analysis, and meta-regression, which was employed to address heterogeneity. The pooled prevalence of SCZ in people with MS was 0.61% (95% CI, 0.25%-1.11%), and BD was 3.34% (95% CI, 2.04%-4.91%). Leave-one-out analyses showed minimal to mild variation in both estimates. The prevalence of BD was higher in people with early-stage MS or moderate disability and varied by sex ratio. For both SCZ and BD, significant geographic differences were identified, with higher prevalence reported in the Americas and Europe. The study period influenced both SCZ and BD prevalences, although study design affected BD estimates and diagnostic approach influenced SCZ. The meta-regression identified study period, sample size, sex ratio, and diagnostic method as sources of heterogeneity in BD, although SCZ heterogeneity was driven by diagnostic method and prevalence type. SCZ and BD are clinically relevant comorbidities in people with MS, with significant heterogeneity across studies driven by various factors. BD appears to be more prevalent in people with early-stage MS and in those with moderate disability. These findings highlight the need for standardized assessments and further studies.

title: Transient and Immediate Motor Effects of Endurance Training in People With Multiple Sclerosis: The Exploratory TIME Study.
abstract: People with multiple sclerosis (MS) occasionally report deterioration of motor function after endurance training. Endurance training is recommended to help manage MS symptoms, but its immediate impact on functional mobility and spasticity is not well understood. Therefore, the aim of this exploratory pre/post analysis was to investigate the immediate effects of a single bout of endurance training on a bicycle ergometer on functional mobility and lower extremity spasticity in people with MS. Forty people with MS (21 men and 19 women; Expanded Disability Status Scale score ≤ 6.0) were randomly assigned to perform either a single bout of high-intensity interval training (HIIT) or moderate continuous training (MCT) on a bicycle ergometer. Functional mobility and spasticity were assessed using the Timed Up and Go (TUG), Numeric Rating Scale for Spasticity (NRS-S), and Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS) at 5 timepoints: before exercise, up to 5 minutes after exercise, at 60 minutes, 180 minutes, and 300 minutes after exercise. A significant decline in functional mobility, as measured by the TUG ( The findings of this study can be used to reassure patients that acute, exercise-related symptom worsening is short-lived and to inform them about the time course to performance and symptom recovery to baseline, or even beyond.

title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Initial Efficacy of a Wheelchair Exercise Training Program in People With Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Exercise training is established as an effective approach for secondary and tertiary prevention among people with multiple sclerosis (MS); however, there are currently no evidence-based exercise training programs for people with MS who use wheelchairs. A 3-step, community-engaged research process was initiated to develop an exercise training intervention to help people with MS who use wheelchairs manage the consequences of MS and optimize their health. The current study investigated the feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary efficacy of the novel program. Twenty-four participants were enrolled, and 23 were randomly assigned into the 16-week exercise intervention or a wellness control condition. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment and retention rates as well as safety. Acceptability outcomes included postintervention surveys and semistructured interviews to measure participant satisfaction and perceptions. Efficacy outcomes included changes in metabolic health biomarkers, in self-reported MS symptoms, and in self-reported and device-measured physical activity behavior. Participant satisfaction was high across both conditions (4.5 and 4.6 out of 5). We conducted a rapid qualitative data analysis of semistructured interviews on participants' experiences, barriers, and future research interests. Preliminary efficacy outcomes indicated that 50% or more of intervention participants achieved at least a 0.5 SD change in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, total self-reported physical activity, and depression. Only 1 study-related adverse event was reported. The stakeholder-informed exercise training program was feasible, safe, and acceptable among people with MS who use wheelchairs. The results support a larger clinical trial to assess the efficacy of the exercise intervention in improving metabolic health and MS symptoms.

title: Pseudo-Exacerbation in Primary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: A Case Report.
abstract: Primary progressive multiple sclerosis (PPMS) is characterised by gradual neurological deterioration from disease onset without distinct relapses. Acute neurological worsening in patients with PPMS can present a diagnostic challenge, particularly when occurring in the context of systemic infection, where pseudo-relapse may mimic disease progression or a true inflammatory relapse. We report the case of a 65-year-old woman with established PPMS who presented with fever, sore throat, and acute bilateral lower-limb weakness. Assessment included a detailed history, neurological examination, and laboratory investigations demonstrating increased inflammatory markers. Neurology review was undertaken to distinguish pseudo-relapse from true relapse. In the absence of new focal neurological deficits and with a probable infective trigger, the episode was considered a pseudo-relapse secondary to presumed pharyngitis. The patient was treated with empirical antibiotics and supportive rehabilitation without corticosteroids. Significant clinical improvement was observed, with return to baseline mobility and functional status. As no contemporaneous MRI was performed, the diagnosis and treatment were based on clinical grounds. At the two-month follow-up, she remained clinically stable with no new neurological deficits. This case highlights the importance of distinguishing pseudo-relapse from true relapse in patients with PPMS presenting with acute neurological deterioration. Careful clinical assessment and recognition of reversible systemic triggers can help avoid unnecessary corticosteroid exposure while ensuring appropriate management of the underlying cause.

title: Unequal Burden: Sex Differences in Cannabis Withdrawal Symptom Severity in People With Multiple Sclerosis-A Short Report.
abstract: People with multiple sclerosis (MS) frequently use cannabis to manage symptoms such as pain, spasticity, and sleep disturbance. During abstinence, withdrawal symptoms may overlap with MS-related complaints, complicating cessation. This study examined whether cannabis withdrawal trajectories differ by sex during monitored abstinence in people with MS. Nineteen frequent cannabis users with MS (11 women) completed 28 days of monitored abstinence. Withdrawal symptoms were assessed using the Cannabis Withdrawal Questionnaire (CWQ) at baseline and weekly through day 28. Abstinence was verified using creatinine-adjusted urinary THC-COOH ratios. Mood was assessed using the Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale (HADS) at baseline and day 28. A repeated-measures analysis of covariance examined time × sex effects, adjusting for demographic, disability, and cannabis-use covariates. At baseline (preabstinence), women reported higher CWQ scores than men. On day 28, women again showed higher scores. A significant time × sex interaction (Pillai trace = .784; Women with MS demonstrated a more pronounced and sustained increase in CWQ symptom burden over the abstinence period than men. These findings likely reflect both withdrawal-related effects and the unmasking of underlying MS-related symptoms. Cannabis cessation appears psychologically tolerable in people with MS, though women may require closer monitoring and targeted support during abstinence.

title: Comparing Preferences of Men and Women With Multiple Sclerosis for Neurologist-Provided Support.
abstract: Sex and gender may influence the preferences of people with multiple sclerosis (MS) in their interactions with health care professionals. We aimed to identify similarities and differences between men and women with MS in their fulfilled and unmet needs and expectations regarding neurologist-provided support. Survey responses to 3 open-ended questions on neurologist-provided support from the Swiss MS Registry were analyzed using a deductive thematic approach based on an established 5-category social support framework, with responses that did not fit the framework analyzed inductively. Findings were compared between men and women using narrative summaries and counts and frequencies of coded support categories. Six hundred seventy participants contributed 1446 text inputs (372 from 163 men; 1074 from 507 women). Both men and women valued a range of neurologist support, including active listening, clear information, sufficient consultation time, and empathy; men most frequently reported receiving informational support (39.0%), whereas women emphasized both emotional (27.6%) and informational support (26.8%). Overall, 24.5% of men and 17.0% of women reported unmet support needs and expectations, with informational support accounting for nearly two-thirds of men's (65.3%) and one-third of women's (32.9%) unmet needs. Support perceptions may be shaped by diagnostics and therapy, neurologist characteristics, and health care site features, the latter raised exclusively by women. Men and women with MS share core expectations for neurologist support but differ in emphasis, with men prioritizing informational support and women valuing a broader range of support types. Perceptions of support may be influenced by factors related to care context.

title: Mediating and Moderating Factors of the Effect of Psychological Therapies Among People With Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: People living with multiple sclerosis (MS) can experience a range of psychological, emotional, and somatic symptoms. Current literature on psychological therapies for people with MS is limited, particularly regarding mechanisms of action and the characteristics of those likely to benefit. This study identifies mediating and moderating factors involved in the relationship between psychological therapies and outcomes among people with MS. Five major databases were searched for randomized controlled trials comparing any psychological therapy in people with MS. Included studies were compiled and screened for inclusion by mediation and moderation analyses using an a priori list of variables. Mediation and moderation analyses were then conducted, examining pooled mean changes across outcomes (physical, cognitive, psychological, quality of life, feasibility, and health economics). In total, 68 studies were included in mediator analyses and 65 in moderator analyses. In mediation analyses, psychological interventions had a significant direct effect on outcomes regardless of mediator ( These results suggest that individuals' level of education and whether their fatigue has been addressed are important considerations in the use of psychological interventions among people with MS.

title: Cross-Sectional Study of Multiple Sclerosis Nurse Care in Australia: Patterns of Access, Improved Health Outcomes, and Recommendations: Part 1.
abstract: In Australia, multiple sclerosis (MS) specialist nurses are an integral part of the multidisciplinary health care team for people with MS, but does everyone have access to MS nurse care, and is access associated with improved health outcomes? Our aim was to evaluate patterns of access to MS nurse care and associations between MS nurse access and health outcomes. Data were collected from 1417 Australians with MS on MS nurse access and health outcomes, including disability, severity of 13 symptoms, health-related quality of life, and treatment. Regression analyses were used to evaluate associations. Overall, 31.5% of respondents had no access to MS nurse care. Those without access were substantially older, had a longer disease duration, and were more likely to be male, less educated, and live in more remote areas. Multivariable analyses showed that, compared with people with access to MS nurse care, those without access had consistently worse health outcomes, including a higher level of disability, a higher rate of self-reported progression in the past 12 months, a higher severity of all MS symptoms, and a lower health-related quality of life. The effect sizes of the mean ratios ranged from 10% to 24%. A substantial proportion of people with MS in Australia do not have access to MS nurse care and have less favorable health outcomes. Increasing awareness of and access to MS nurse care could promote more effective disease management and improve health outcomes for people with MS.

title: Temporal Change: Evaluation of Brain Atrophy in Patients with Radiologically Isolated Syndrome Using volBrain.
Translational Applications of Retinal Biomarkers in Chronic Cardiovascular, Neurological, Metabolic, and Renal Diseases.
abstract: Imaging the retina is a powerful non-invasive probe of systemic vascular, neurological, metabolic, and renal disease, making it a cornerstone of the new field of systemic oculomics. Advanced retinal imaging techniques like optical coherence tomography (OCT) and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) provide detailed imaging of structural and microvascular changes potentially associated with systemic disease. Derived from fundus photography, structural imaging, vascular imaging, and artificial intelligence-based image analysis, retinal biomarkers have been associated with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease, neurodegenerative disorders, diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and related clinical outcomes. However, the translational maturity of these biomarkers is variable depending on imaging modality, target disease, intended clinical use, and level of validation. Longitudinally, retinal vascular characteristics have been associated with cardiovascular as well as cerebrovascular outcomes. In addition, optical coherence tomography has provided reproducible measures of neuroaxonal injury in selected neurological conditions. This is especially true for multiple sclerosis. The majority of retinal biomarkers in Alzheimer disease, Parkinson disease, chronic kidney disease, and systemic risk prediction remain experimental because of heterogeneous methodologies, insufficient external validation, and insufficient evidence for incremental clinical utility. Diabetes is the most developed translational model with established retinal screening pathways and validated ocular applications of imaging and artificial intelligence, although these cannot be directly extrapolated to systemic diagnosis or treatment guidance. This narrative review assesses retinal biomarkers for cardiovascular, neurological, metabolic, and renal disease with a focus on analytical validity, clinical validity, incremental value, clinical utility, and implementation. The retina is increasingly accepted as a site for discovery of systemic biomarkers and adjunctive risk assessment, although most applications to systemic disease remain to be standardized, validated independently, and studied prospectively before being suitable for routine clinical use.

title: Association of Diagnosis Age with Clinical Characteristics and MRI Findings in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Age at multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis may be associated with clinical course, inflammatory activity, and disability accrual, but evidence across the full age spectrum remains limited. We compared clinical and radiological features, phenotype distribution, and time to first post-diagnosis relapse across early-onset MS (EOMS), adult-onset MS (AOMS), and late-onset MS (LOMS). METHODS: This observational study included patients with MS treated at two tertiary centers in Isfahan, Iran, combining a retrospective review of clinical records with a cross-sectional assessment at the most recent study visit. Patients were categorized as EOMS (MS diagnosis at ≤18 years), AOMS, or LOMS (diagnosis at or after 50 years) according to age at diagnosis. Demographic, clinical, MRI, and comorbidity data were compared across groups. Time to first post-diagnosis relapse was analyzed in RRMS using Cox regression, and continuous age effects were explored with spline models. RESULTS: Among 3994 patients, 257 had EOMS, 3587 had AOMS, and 150 had LOMS. EOMS had a higher hazard of first post-diagnosis relapse (adjusted HR: 1.27, 95% CI: 1.05-1.54) and more frequent enhancing brain lesions. LOMS had a more progressive phenotype, higher EDSS at diagnosis and qualitative brain atrophy, and more age-associated comorbidities. The adjusted LOMS relapse estimate (HR: 0.58, 95% CI: 0.34-0.99) was borderline significant. Progressive MS became more common with increasing diagnosis age, largely reflecting PPMS, although unequal follow-up and last-visit classification limit causal interpretation. Female predominance persisted across all groups but was less pronounced in LOMS. CONCLUSIONS: Age at diagnosis was associated with clinical and radiological differences across the MS spectrum from a more relapsing phenotype to a more progressive, disability-associated phenotype. These findings should be verified in prospective studies based on symptomatic onset age.

title: From Association to Action: Personalizing Lifestyle Interventions in Multiple Sclerosis-A Critical Narrative Review.
abstract: Lifestyle factors are increasingly incorporated into multiple sclerosis (MS) care, but association, modifiability and therapeutic justification are not equivalent. This critical narrative review examines when a lifestyle exposure should become a clinical target after MS diagnosis. Evidence across physical activity and exercise, smoking, obesity and cardiometabolic health, diet, sleep, psychological stress, vitamin D and sun exposure, cognitive reserve and engagement, and alcohol is interpreted through the sequence modifiable exposure → post-diagnostic prognostic relevance → deliberate intervention → verified target modification (target engagement) → demonstrated clinical benefit, while distinguishing general-health benefit, MS-relevant clinical benefit and evidence for MS disease-course modification. The strength and completeness of this evidence vary substantially across domains. Smoking cessation and physical activity provide particularly strong grounds for clinical action, whereas several other exposures show larger gaps between prognostic association and intervention evidence. Multidomain intervention is not inherently personalized; personalization requires selection and prioritization of targets according to the intended outcome, strength of evidence, individual relevance and feasibility, followed by verification that the target changed and that the expected benefit occurred. Lifestyle intervention should complement, not substitute for, disease-modifying therapy, and no MS-directed intervention may be the appropriate personalized decision when a clinically relevant or sufficiently supported target is absent. The objective is therefore to support proportionate lifestyle decisions in which the intervention, intended outcome and therapeutic claim are matched to the available evidence and the individual clinical context.

title: A Blood-Based Synaptic Biomarker in Neuronally-Enriched Extracellular Vesicles Predicts Disability Progression in Progressive Multiple Sclerosis.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
abstract: Progressive multiple sclerosis (PMS) lacks blood-based biomarkers of the neurodegenerative processes driving disability. We measured synaptopodin, a postsynaptic protein, in neuronal-enriched extracellular vesicles (NEVs) across two independent cohorts: the SPRINT-MS trial (n=184) and a real-world validation cohort (n=268). A one SD increase in baseline synaptopodin was associated with ∼32% lower risk of confirmed disability progression in PMS (p=0.011), with the strongest effect in secondary PMS (SPMS) (∼57% lower odds, p=0.019). This SPMS association was replicated in the validation cohort (∼60% lower odds, p=0.009). Higher baseline synaptopodin was associated with future slower whole-brain atrophy and preserved microstructural integrity across MRI metrics (p=0.007-0.013). Longitudinal changes in NEV synaptopodin were associated with disability worsening (p=0.007) and paralleled MRI microstructural changes. NEV synaptopodin, but not NfL, was associated with confirmed disability progression in PMS participants with both biomarkers measured (HR 0.71 vs 1.12, p=0.007 vs 0.22 for NEV synaptopodin and NfL, respectively) and SPMS (HR 0.58 vs 1.10, p=0.003 vs 0.50). Adding synaptopodin, but not NfL, to a base model improved discrimination for disability progression in SPMS in both cohorts (e.g. validation AUC 0.755 to 0.838, p=0.005). These findings identify NEV synaptopodin as a prognostic and longitudinal, blood biomarker of synaptic integrity in PMS, particularly SPMS, complementing NfL.

title: Label-Free Acoustic Wave Detection of Myelin Basic Protein for Monitoring of Neurodegenerative Disease.
abstract: Myelin basic protein (MBP) is released into cerebrospinal fluid during demyelination and is therefore a promising biomarker for the detection of neurodegenerative diseases such as multiple sclerosis. For the label-free detection of MBP, we developed an antifouling aptasensor based on thickness shear mode sensing. DNA aptamers were immobilized on gold-coated piezoelectric crystals functionalized with an engineered antifouling self-assembled monolayer based on 3-(2-mercaptoethoxy)propanoic acid (HS-MEG-COOH) combined with either 2-(2-mercaptoethoxy)ethanol (HS-MEG-OH) or dithiothreitol (DTT) as spacers. The binding of recombinant human MBP to the aptamer was confirmed with a corresponding decrease in resonance frequency in both phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and artificial cerebrospinal fluid (aCSF). The aptasensor achieved a limit of detection of 11 ng mL-1 in PBS and 2 ng mL-1 in aCSF. PBS measurements were primarily applied to determine the aptasensor functionality, whereas experiments in aCSF evaluated MBP detection at concentrations relevant to reported levels in biological CSF. Selectivity was assessed with aptamer-free surfaces, cytochrome c, and human serum albumin (HSA) with much lower responses, while concentration-dependent MBP detection was maintained in aCSF despite the increased complexity of the matrix. The antifouling performance of the modified sensing surface was further demonstrated in aCSF by the significantly reduced frequency and dissipation responses compared to bare gold. With future validation in human cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples, the developed biosensor has the potential to enable sensitive, label-free detection of MBP in CSF for the identification and monitoring of neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Real-world evidence of diagnosis, treatment, and disease characteristics among Japanese patients with multiple sclerosis: The Multiple Sclerosis Epidemiological Retrospective Japan (MSERJ) study.
abstract: Nationwide data for patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) in Japan, including the sequence of disease-modifying therapy (DMT), are limited. The MS Epidemiological Retrospective Japan (MSERJ) study examined disease characteristics and DMT patterns among Japanese patients with MS. This multicenter study conducted at 20 specialist MS centers examined retrospective data from patients with clinically or radiologically isolated syndrome (CIS/RIS), relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS), secondary progressive MS (SPMS), or primary progressive MS (PPMS) between June 2022 and May 2023. The primary endpoint was the annualized relapse rate (ARR) over 2 years. Of 842 patients, the number with RRMS, SPMS, PPMS, and CIS was 685 (81.4%), 77 (9.1%), 62 (7.4%), and six (0.7%), respectively. In RRMS patients, the ARR was 0.12; risk factors for increased ARR were younger age at onset, shorter MS duration, and shorter DMT duration; no DMT use at final visit was potentially associated, although significance was not consistently observed. Between 2011 and 2014 and 2020-2023, the median time from onset to diagnosis (6.2 vs 2.1 months; p < 0.001) and from diagnosis to first DMT (4.3 vs 1.4 months; p < 0.001) was shortened. The proportion of patients receiving DMT increased over time from 52.1% in 2011-2014 to 89.2% in 2020-2023, with rates for high-efficacy DMTs also increasing (from 1.4% to 31.7%). Japanese patients with MS treated at specialist MS centers had a relatively low ARR, with significantly shortened time to diagnosis and DMT initiation, and increased DMT usage rates over time, particularly high-efficacy DMTs.

title: A Feasible Machine Learning Approach to Improve Cognitive Screening in Multiple Sclerosis.
Effectiveness of Native and Enhanced Extracellular Vesicle Preparations Assessed in Animal Models of Multiple Sclerosis: A Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Extracellular vesicle (EV) preparations have emerged as potentially useful therapeutic tools for various inflammatory or neurodegenerative CNS disorders. Compared to mesenchymal stem cell preparations, they feature enhanced blood-brain barrier permeability and access to injured brain tissue, and better quality assessment and dosing options. A particular case where such therapies may prove beneficial is multiple sclerosis (MS), an autoimmune disease likely triggered by cross-reactivity with some viral antigens, producing an extended demyelinating encephalomyelitis with multiple patchy lesions. Several animal models of MS have been developed, including experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) via injection of myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG) 35-55, inoculation with Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus (TMEV), and the Cuprizone model. Via literature search we retrieved 24 experimental studies on rodent (rat or mouse) MS models with therapeutic administration of native or enhanced EV preparations suitable for this meta-analysis. We found statistically significant mean differences between experimental and control groups for clinical scores (normalized to a 0-5 scale) (-1.21, 95% confidence interval (CI) [-1.49,-0.93] (native EVs); -1.67, CI [-2.28,-1.05] (enhanced EVs)), for pathological scores of inflammation and demyelination, and for several molecular markers of inflammation and myelin repair. These results point to the need for clinical translation of the encouraging preliminary results obtained using such MS animal models.

title: Lack of Association Between CAT rs1001179 and SOD2 rs4880 Variants and Risk for Multiple Sclerosis.
Unveiling Asymptomatic Atrioventricular Reciprocating Tachycardia in a Patient With Wolff-Parkinson-White Syndrome and Multiple Sclerosis.
journal: The American journal of case reports
abstract: BACKGROUND Intermittent accessory pathway conduction can obscure the electrocardiographic diagnosis of Wolff-Parkinson-White (WPW) syndrome on resting electrocardiograms (ECGs). Furthermore, sensory disruptions characteristic of multiple sclerosis (MS) can blunt symptom perception, masking potentially life-threatening hemodynamic instability. CASE REPORT A 54-year-old woman with secondary-progressive MS (SPMS) was admitted for a complicated urinary tract infection. The admitting ECG demonstrated sinus tachycardia without preexcitation. Telemetry subsequently revealed narrow-complex tachycardia at 220 beats per minute (BPM) with concurrent hypotension. Despite hemodynamic instability, the patient explicitly denied palpitations, chest pain, or presyncope. She had discontinued fingolimod several years earlier because of palpitations, a detail retrospectively suggestive of an accessory pathway. Review of records identified historical ECGs with intermittent delta waves and short PR intervals, confirming the presence of an accessory pathway with intermittent antegrade conduction. A 12-lead ECG during the acute event confirmed orthodromic atrioventricular reciprocating tachycardia (AVRT). The patient underwent successful synchronized cardioversion followed by radiofrequency ablation of a left-sided anterolateral accessory pathway via electrophysiological study (EPS). CONCLUSIONS This case illustrates the "ECG dilemma" of intermittent preexcitation, in which the absence of delta waves on a resting tracing does not exclude accessory pathway-mediated tachycardia. It further highlights that patients with neuro-modulating diseases, such as MS, may lack classical "alarm" symptoms for arrhythmia due to progressive autonomic and sensory dysfunction. Clinicians must maintain a high index of suspicion for concealed arrhythmias in this population, as neurological impairment can dissociate hemodynamic instability from subjective symptom perception. Objective monitoring with telemetry is essential to prevent adverse outcomes in this vulnerable population.

title: Host genomic context determines the direction of an oracle-predicted sequence effect: a composition-preserving CpG intervention in Enformer and Borzoi.
abstract: Sequence-to-function models are increasingly used as oracles to score designed regulatory elements, on the untested assumption that an effect measured at one locus holds at another. Taking chromatin and host loci from multiple sclerosis risk regions, we kept four questions apart: sequence realism, transfer of discrimination, edit stability, calibration. A sixth-order Markov chain reproduced the cell-type-specific motif enrichment a trained transformer missed, despite its lower held-out likelihood. Scores differ in level between loci far more than between inserts at one locus, yet inserts selected by an Enformer-derived index kept 85% of their advantage at four unseen loci. Once GC was matched, however, the index separated peak-derived from inaccessible sequence at none of 12 hosts, and from random sequence in opposite directions at different hosts. Placing identical inserts and an identical CpG edit at 24 host loci, the effect varied far beyond sampling noise on host identity alone ([Formula: see text]), unpredicted by 18 host properties. It survives scoring only the bins the insert occupies ([Formula: see text], and across 200 loci), so is no artefact of aggregation; the apparent host dominance, however, falls from 25-fold to 3-fold under that localised score, and the one locus positive under the whole-window score reverses under it. Borzoi reproduced the heterogeneity but not its amplitude, and the objective did not predict lentiMPRA activity. For these two oracles and this edit, the size of a predicted effect depends on where it is measured, and its direction at any one locus is not robust.

title: Pathophysiology of Neuropathic Pain in Multiple Sclerosis: a Review.
abstract: Neuropathic pain is one of the most relevant symptoms in multiple sclerosis (MS) and is a key contributor to the impaired quality of life in this disease. A better understanding of MS-related neuropathic pain is needed to develop new drugs and improve the use of available ones. In this review, we cover existing knowledge on the pathophysiology of neuropathic pain in patients with MS. Our current understanding of this disorder stems from studies conducted on MS, other diseases responsible for neuropathic pain, and animal models of demyelinating disorders, like experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis. Responsible mechanisms are complex and can act at different levels. At the molecular and cellular scale, neuronal hyperexcitability is the main driver of neuropathic pain; it is the final consequence of other interacting events taking place on the cell membrane and in the intracellular and extracellular environment. Impairment of inhibitory neurotransmission further enhances hyperexcitability. Functional alterations of complex neuronal networks can be observed at higher levels, showing that modifications of the dynamic pain connectome play a relevant role in the pathogenesis of pain. Moreover, in recent years a distinction has been drawn between neuropathic and nociplastic pain; the consequences of this new classification on pathophysiological models of MS-related neuropathic pain are not still fully understood and deserve future attention.

title: ESR Essentials: susceptibility-weighted imaging-practice recommendations by the European Society for Magnetic Resonance in Medicine and Biology.
abstract: Susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI) is a high-resolution 3D gradient-echo (GRE) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) technique that combines magnitude and phase information to increase sensitivity to blood products, iron, calcification, thrombus, and venous structures. In routine practice, SWI should be interpreted together with source magnitude images, filtered phase images, processed SWI images, and minimum-intensity projection (minIP) images, keeping in mind blooming and other artefacts, as well as vendor-dependent phase conventions. Its most established role is in brain MRI, particularly in: suspected cerebral amyloid angiopathy; baseline and follow-up assessment of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities with haemosiderin deposition (ARIA-H) during anti-amyloid therapy; traumatic brain injury; multiple sclerosis work-up, when assessment of the central vein sign or paramagnetic rim lesions is clinically relevant; neuro-oncology; and vascular malformations. Overall, these constitute the core recommended brain scenarios for SWI supported by moderate to high levels of evidence. Outside neuroradiology (e.g., musculoskeletal, abdominal, breast, pelvic, and cardiac imaging), SWI remains promising but less standardised and should currently be reserved for selected problem-solving indications. KEY POINTS: SWI should be acquired as a high-resolution 3D GRE sequence and interpreted together with source magnitude images, filtered phase images, and post-processed minIP images, keeping in mind blooming and other artefacts, as well as vendor-specific phase conventions. SWI should be included in brain MRI protocols when haemorrhagic or microvascular susceptibility findings are expected to affect diagnosis or management, especially in cerebral amyloid angiopathy, anti-amyloid therapy monitoring, traumatic brain injury, and neuro-oncology or multiple sclerosis work-up. Outside neuroradiology, SWI can be used as a targeted problem-solving adjunct rather than as a routine sequence.

title: Writer's Cramp: A Presenting Symptom of Demyelinating Disease.
Clinical approach to balance intensity in people with multiple sclerosis: clinical judgment versus the Balance Intensity Tool for Exercise - an inter-rater agreement and reliability study.
abstract: Balance training is essential for enhancing stability in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS). However, guidance on exercise intensity remains vague and largely relies on clinical judgment as standardized assessment methods are absent. This study introduces and evaluates the Balance Intensity Tool for Exercise (BITE), a standardized method for assessment of balance intensity based on observable errors, and compares it with traditional clinical judgment. Sixty-one PwMS, recruited from physiotherapy clinics and social networks, performed two balance tasks: line-walking and tandem-stance. The tasks were videorecorded for subsequent intensity assessment. Intensity was rated using (1) BITE, where three assessors measured the percentage of time with observable errors as a measure of intensity, and (2) clinical judgment, where three experienced physiotherapists scored intensity on a 0-100 scale. Balance capacity was measured with the Mini-BESTest. BITE assessors and clinicians were blinded to each other's ratings. Inter-rater agreement, reliability, and measurement error were evaluated using Bland-Altman analysis with 95% Limits of Agreement (LoA), Intra-class Correlation Coefficient (ICC Intensities measured by BITE were consistently lower than clinical judgment (line-walking median: 36% vs. 74%; tandem-stance median: 23% vs. 53%). BITE demonstrated excellent inter‑rater reliability (ICC BITE provides a quantifiable method to describe balance exercise intensity in PwMS based on the time of observed performance errors. BITE demonstrated excellent inter-rater reliability and inter-rater agreement, with LoA ≤ 20%, while clinical judgment exhibited wider LoA. Further research should explore its applicability in other populations with impaired balance.

title: Processing speed test as an alternative to the symbol digit modalities test for cognitive screening in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: To replicate previous findings on the validity of the Processing Speed Test (PST) as a potential alternative to the Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) for assessing neurocognitive function in patients with multiple sclerosis (MS), and to further confirm its associations with demographic, clinical, neuropsychological, radiological, and sociodemographic factors. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 219 adults diagnosed with relapsing remitting MS. Cognitive assessment included the Brief International Cognitive Assessment for MS (BICAMS) battery-comprising SDMT, California Verbal Learning Test, and Brief Visuospatial Memory Test-Revised-alongside the PST, which is self-administered on a digital device. Fatigue and mood were measured using the Modified Fatigue Impact Scale and Beck Depression Inventory-Second Edition (BDI-II), respectively. Also clinical, demographic, and magnetic resonance image variables were collected. Correlations between PST, SDMT, and other cognitive, demographic, clinical and radiological measures were calculated. PST exhibited a strong positive correlation with SDMT (rho=0.814, p < 0.001) and similar associations with other BICAMS subtests. Lower PST scores were associated with older age higher fatigue, depression, disability, and lesion burden; while higher educational level was linked to better performance. These findings replicate and strengthen prior evidence supporting the PST as a valid cognitive screening tool in MS. Its self-administered and automated scoring supports its use as a practical alternative to SDMT for routine clinical screening. Further longitudinal studies are needed to confirm its utility for monitoring cognitive changes over time.

title: Transcription factor EB as a novel target for dimethyl fumarate to restore endothelial function in diabetes.
abstract: Diabetes mellitus-associated endothelial dysfunction represents a pivotal early event in diabetic vasculopathy, linking metabolic derangements to vascular injury. Dimethyl fumarate (DMF), an FDA-approved drug for multiple sclerosis and psoriasis, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, yet whether it protects against diabetic endothelial dysfunction and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, diabetic db/db mice and the non-diabetic db/m

title: Targeting Mitochondrial Redox Signaling Promotes Neuroregeneration and Functional Recovery in a Multiple Sclerosis Model.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, including multiple sclerosis (MS), are characterized by progressive neuronal loss and limited regenerative capacity. To stimulate in vivo neurogenesis and oligodendrogenesis by harnessing the untapped regenerative potential of endogenous neural progenitor cells (NPCs) that are upregulated in the CNS under disease conditions, we developed a novel compound that targets Notch signaling, a pathway known to suppress neuronal differentiation of NPCs. Furapyrrodole, which was identified by screening a natural product-like synthetic chemical library, binds to and activates the mitochondrial reductase CYB5R3, which naturally downregulates Notch signaling downstream of γ-secretase. The in vivo efficacy of furapyrrodole was evaluated in mice with experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), a mouse model of MS. Furapyrrodole treatment after the peak of EAE disease significantly improved motor function and promoted recovery of motor neurons and myelination by stimulating endogenous NPC-derived neurogenesis and oligodendrogenesis. In addition, furapyrrodole supresses neuroinflammation in the CNS. Collectively, these findings indicate furapyrrodole is a promising therapeutic candidate for MS by harnessing endogenously upregulated NPCs and inducing anti-inflammation. Our study demonstrates for the first time that modulation of mitochondrial redox signaling promotes neuroregeneration and remyelination without causing severe adverse effects.

title: Plasma and CSF neurofilament light chain measured by Simoa and Lumipulse: an inter-platform comparison across neurological disorders.
abstract: Blood neurofilament light chain (NfL) is an accessible biomarker of neuroaxonal injury, but clinical implementation requires robust analytical comparability across platforms. We evaluated plasma NfL measured by Simoa and Lumipulse across neurological disorders, including paired CSF analyses to anchor plasma findings to the central compartment. We included 383 individuals, comprising healthy controls and patients with neurodegenerative diseases, multiple sclerosis, and ischemic stroke. Plasma NfL was measured in all participants using Simoa and Lumipulse; paired CSF measurements were available in 92 individuals. Lumipulse intermediate precision and between-day repeatability were assessed according to CLSI EP15. Cross-platform agreement was evaluated using Spearman correlation, Passing-Bablok regression, and Bland-Altman analysis. Plasma-CSF associations and age-adjusted diagnostic differences were assessed separately for each platform. Plasma NfL measured by Simoa and Lumipulse showed strong concordance in the whole cohort (ρ=0.90), with similarly strong CSF concordance in paired samples (ρ=0.90). Method-comparison analyses demonstrated constant and proportional bias, with systematically higher absolute plasma NfL values measured by Lumipulse. Plasma and CSF NfL were significantly correlated within each platform (ρ=0.72 for Simoa; ρ=0.77 for Lumipulse). Lumipulse blood and CSF assays showed high precision. Across both platforms, plasma NfL increased with age and was higher in neurological disorders than in healthy controls. Simoa and Lumipulse capture a consistent plasma NfL signal across neurological disorders, but absolute concentrations differ, supporting platform-specific, age-aware interpretation in clinical practice.

title: Effect of electrical stimulation on remyelination in preclinical models of multiple sclerosis: A systematic review.
abstract: Different types of electrical stimulations (ES), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), vagus nerve stimulation (VNS), and peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS) have emerged as neuromodulatory treatments to promote remyelination in multiple sclerosis (MS). Although preclinical evidence continues to accumulate, a systematic review assessing the effect of ES on remyelination across MS-relevant models has not been undertaken. PubMed-MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus databases were systematically searched up to January 2026 for in vivo studies investigating ES in demyelinating animal models. Two reviewers independently extracted data on study design, stimulation parameters, and quantitative measures of myelin integrity, including visual evoked potential (VEP) latency, and histological myelin content outcomes. Risk of bias was assessed using SYRCLE's tool. Six eligible studies met the inclusion criteria, comprising EAE, cuprizone, and lysolecithin lesion models. Across these studies, ES was associated with improvements in indices of remyelination, evidenced by reduced VEP latency, and increased myelin protein expression. Effects of tDCS depended on polarity and timing, with anodal stimulation supporting oligodendrocyte maturation during recovery and cathodal stimulation attenuating glial activation during inflammation. VNS promoted remyelination through anti-inflammatory and trophic signaling, and PNS supported spinal remyelination via peripheral to central neuroimmune modulation. Limited but convergent preclinical evidence suggests ES may enhance remyelination by modulating neuronal and inflammatory pathways. However, standardized protocols of stimulation and multimodal imaging studies are needed for clinical translation in MS.

title: Subcutaneous panniculitis-like T cell lymphoma in a patient with multiple sclerosis during anti-CD20 therapy: a case report.
Blood Cell Imaging Analysis for Multiple Sclerosis Classification Using Leave-One-Subject-Out Study with Deep Neural Networks.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disease whose diagnosis typically relies on resource-intensive and partly invasive procedures such as MRI and spinal fluid analysis. This study explores whether deep learning can identify distinguishing patterns in RBC images associated with MS, aiming to determine whether blood-cell imaging may provide information relevant to understanding the disease. The initial dataset comprised 121 images from 13 independent subjects. To expand the dataset to 1944 images, image augmentation techniques were applied to the training data to increase image variability. Due to the small dataset, training was carried out using a Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) strategy to assess model performance on unseen subjects. Four deep learning architectures, VGG16, DenseNet201, MobileNetV2, and the Swin Transformer, were evaluated using subject-level Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV). The Swin Transformer achieved the highest mean accuracy (73.53%), followed by the fully fine-tuned VGG16 (71.02%). Explainable AI techniques (Grad-CAM and SWTformer-v1) applied to the given dataset showed that VGG16 focused on broader structural patterns in cell groupings, while SWTformer-v1 attended to more localized regions. These findings suggest that deep-learning models can identify distinguishing image patterns that contribute to classifying RBC images from MS and healthy controls. The XAI analyses further provide insight into the image regions the models use, although their biological relevance requires validation in larger cohorts.

title: Serum neurofilament light chain and the 2024 McDonald criteria for multiple sclerosis: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: The 2024 McDonald criteria broaden the definition of multiple sclerosis (MS), enabling diagnosis in individuals with asymptomatic MRI findings or clinical presentations not meeting the 2017 criteria. We assessed whether these criteria identify such cases using independent laboratory/imaging biomarkers and whether these biomarkers predict subsequent disease activity. Participants with asymptomatic MRI findings or clinical presentations not meeting the 2017 criteria were included and stratified according to the 2024 criteria. Serum neurofilament light chain (sNfL) and 3T brain MRI measures-including normalised brain volumes, T2 lesion load (T2LL), cortical lesion (CL) and paramagnetic rim lesion (PRL)-were compared between McDonald2024-positive and McDonald2024-negative groups, and with age/sex matched McDonald2017-positive cases according to the 2017 criteria; predictors of disease activity were assessed using penalised-Cox regression. A total of 141 participants were included: 95 not meeting the 2017 criteria (n = 64 asymptomatic MRI findings; n = 31 clinical presentations), stratified as McDonald2024-positive (n = 46) or McDonald2024-negative (n = 49), and 46 McDonald2017-positive cases. McDonald2024-positive vs. McDonald2024-negative cases showed higher age-corrected sNfL Z-scores (median 0.28[IQR 0.76] vs. -0.12[0.82], p = 0.003/pFDR = 0.006), reduced normalised thalamic volume (mean 0.009±[SD]0.0007 vs. 0.010 ± 0.0007, p = 0.003/pFDR = 0.006), and higher CL (1[4] vs. 0[0], p < 0.001/pFDR < 0.001) and PRL (1[1] vs. 0[0], p < 0.001/pFDR = 0.003) counts (differences remaining significant after age/sex, disease duration and T2LL adjustments). Biomarker profiles were comparable between McDonald2024-positive and McDonald2017-positive cases. Penalised-Cox regression (n = 52) identified sNfL Z-score and PRL presence as the most consistently selected predictors of disease activity, with higher bootstrap stability for sNfL (0.84) than PRL (0.76), and good model discrimination (C-index = 0.71). The 2024 McDonald criteria identify individuals not meeting the 2017 criteria who already exhibit MS-like neuroinflammatory/neurodegenerative pathological changes. These are reflected by laboratory and imaging biomarkers, including sNfL, which may predict subsequent disease activity and complement current diagnostic frameworks to support early clinical decision-making. title: How interoception shapes body representations in multiple sclerosis.
journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology
abstract: Both interoception and body representations (BR) are frequently altered in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS). However, whether distinct dimensions of interoception differentially impact action-oriented (aBR) and non-action-oriented body representations (NaBR) remains unexplored. To characterize the specific associations between objective and subjective dimensions of interoception and BR components in PwMS compared to healthy controls (HC). Fifty-nine PwMS and 51 HC completed validated assessments of interoceptive accuracy (IAc), sensibility (ISe), and awareness (IAw). BR was evaluated using the Hand Laterality Task (HLT) for aBR and the Frontal Body Evocation (FBE) Task for NaBR. Correlation and regression analyses were performed with Bonferroni correction. After strict multiple-comparison correction, higher interoceptive sensibility (SAQ Total Score) significantly predicted poorer accuracy on the HLT in PwMS. No significant correlations survived correction in the HC group. Exploratory analyses in PwMS suggested an uncorrected disease-specific link between higher IAc and higher deviation and shorter response times in the FBE task. Distinct dimensions of interoception are differentially linked to specific BR components in MS. Subjective body-signal monitoring selectively impairs action-oriented body schema functioning, supporting a multidimensional model of bodily dysfunction.

title: The effects of stretching interventions in people with multiple sclerosis: a systematic review.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disorder of the central nervous system marked by heterogeneous symptoms including spasticity and flexibility limitations. This systematic review investigates the effects of stretching (ST) interventions on physical function and health-related outcomes in people with MS (PwMS). Scopus, NLM PubMed, and Web of Science (Core Collection) were searched through December 2025. Studies evaluating ST in PwMS were included. Methodological quality was assessed using a modified Downs and Black checklist, and certainty of evidence using the GRADE framework. Seven studies involving 144 participants (44.5 ± 9.6 years) were included. Across acute and longitudinal studies, descriptively favorable changes following ST were observed, with several outcomes meeting/exceeding previously published minimal important/detectable change thresholds for Timed Up and Go, flexibility, spasticity, pain, and fatigue. Downs and Black assessment indicated moderate methodological quality. GRADE suggested very low certainty of evidence. ST appears well tolerated and may improve flexibility while also being potentially associated with clinically meaningful improvements in mobility, spasticity, pain, and fatigue in PwMS. However, current evidence remains limited, with ST frequently serving as an active comparator or control rather than the primary intervention, precluding definitive clinical recommendations and underscoring the need for well-designed randomized controlled trials.

title: Effect of square-stepping exercises on mobility, balance and knee joint position sense in individuals with multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is associated with impaired mobility, balance, and lower-limb position sense. This study aimed to investigate the effects of Square-Stepping Exercise (SSE), a task-oriented sensorimotor stepping intervention, on mobility, balance, and knee joint position sense (JPS) in people with MS. Forty individuals with MS, aged 20-50 years, were randomly allocated (1:1) to either the SSE group ( Baseline-adjusted analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) revealed significant between-group differences favoring SSE, with large effect sizes, for T25FW ( The SSE intervention was associated with favorable changes in mobility, balance, and knee JPS outcomes in individuals with MS. This trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05682963) on December 24, 2022.

title: Anti-CD20 mediated B cell depletion exerts a distinct influence on T cell immunity by decreasing effector memory CD4 Th17 and Th1.17 subsets in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is driven by dysregulated B and T cell interactions. Anti-CD20 B cell depletion with rituximab (RTX) strongly suppresses MS disease activity, yet how it relates to T cell immunity is unclear. We analysed clinically acquired flow cytometry data from 310 people with MS before and six months after RTX initiation, with plasma proteomics and CD4 T cell receptor sequencing in subgroups. Baseline T cell profiles correlated with B cell numbers, age, and HLA-DRB1*15:01 status. To limit confounding from prior therapies, RTX-associated changes were primarily assessed in treatment-naïve participants, in whom effector memory Th17 and Th1.17 CD4 subsets were selectively reduced, while CD8 subsets, the plasma inflammatory proteome, and CD4 clonality were largely unchanged. This observational study cannot establish causality, but identifies distinct memory CD4 subsets, relevant to MS disease activity, that are measurable in routine clinical flow cytometry.

title: Editorial for "Monitoring Remyelination and Its Association With Disability Improvement in Multiple Sclerosis Using APART-QSM MRI: A Longitudinal Cohort Study".
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI

title: Expected stigma and life satisfaction in multiple sclerosis: The mediating role of psychological and social well-being.
abstract: This study examined the mediating role of psychological and social well-being in the relationship between anticipated stigma and life satisfaction in individuals with MS. The sample included 495 MS patients aged 18 and older, recruited via convenience sampling. Data were collected using validated scales for anticipated stigma, psychological well-being, social well-being, and life satisfaction. Analyses were conducted with SPSS 25 and PROCESS Macro (Model 4), with anticipated stigma as the independent variable, life satisfaction as the dependent variable, and psychological and social well-being as mediators. title: Ocrelizumab treatment and disability progression in non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic or Latino individuals with relapsing multiple sclerosis: A post hoc analysis of the OPERA I and II trials.
abstract: Racial and ethnic disparities are evident in multiple sclerosis. To assess whether disease progression and treatment response differ between non-Hispanic Black or Hispanic/Latino and non-Hispanic White people with relapsing multiple sclerosis. This post hoc analysis included people with relapsing multiple sclerosis from ocrelizumab trials (NCT01247324/NCT01412333) self-reporting as non-Hispanic Black ( In the interferon beta-1a treatment arm, non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic/Latino people with relapsing multiple sclerosis had increased 24-week cCDP risk compared with non-Hispanic White people with relapsing multiple sclerosis (hazard ratio (95% confidence interval) non-Hispanic Black: 3.0 (1.4-6.5); Compared with non-Hispanic White people, non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic/Latino people with relapsing multiple sclerosis showed higher disease progression risk. Ocrelizumab reduced composite confirmed disability progression risk in people with relapsing multiple sclerosis regardless of race, ethnicity, or genetic ancestry.

title: 'I didn't want to face my future': Experiences of social participation among people living with progressive neurological conditions.
abstract: Social participation is important for health and wellbeing, particularly for people living with progressive neurological conditions. This study explored experiences of social participation among adults with conditions including Parkinson's disease, multiple sclerosis and Huntington's disease, alongside perspectives from health and social care professionals and community activity organisers in Wales, United Kingdom. title: Neuroinflammatory Biomarkers in Neurodegenerative Disease Diagnosis and Progression.
abstract: Neuroinflammatory markers are now key tools for diagnosing and monitoring neurodegenerative diseases. These biomarkers are associated with the activation of the immune system in the central nervous system, which is associated with the disease process. This review highlights some selected aspects of the neuroinflammatory markers, cytokines, chemokines, and markers of glial activation, and their role in diseases such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and multiple sclerosis. Recent innovations in molecular and imaging technology have led to better identification and measurement of neuroinflammatory biomarkers in CSF, blood, and brain tissue. These approaches allow noninvasive monitoring and assist in the integration of biomarker profiles coupled with clinical evaluation for better diagnostic accuracy and patient stratification. Fluctuations in neuroinflammatory markers are associated with disease activity and cognitive impairment, which suggest these markers as potential early diagnostic and prognostic indicators. Using a biomarker profile in addition to clinical information helps better distinguish among neurodegenerative disorders and monitor therapeutic outcomes. Although promising, challenges remain in standardising biomarker measurement and interpreting biomarker specificity, given overlapping inflammatory pathways between diseases. There is ongoing research to confirm biomarker panels that can reliably differentiate between neurodegenerative disorders and track treatment effects. Decoding the multifaceted crosstalk between neuroinflammation and neurodegeneration is essential for developing targeted therapies that modulate immune processes and slow disease progression. Neuroinflammatory biomarkers are useful diagnostic and prognostic tools that can aid in the clinical management and the development of new treatment strategies in neurodegenerative disorders.

title: Integrated NULISA-based CSF neuroimmune profiling identifies microglial-axonal injury signatures and their clinical and MRI associations in new-onset Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is characterized by inflammatory demyelination, neuroaxonal injury and progressive neurodegeneration. The biological processes driving the disease are already active at clinical onset, yet comprehensive characterization of different molecular pathways at diagnosis remains limited.
