Predicting covariables included age (< /≥ 45 years), pre-baseline activity, and short-term NEDA-3 status regarding 3YFS outcomes beyond year 3 (long-term). ARR declined significantly from ~0.55 in the year pre-baseline to ~0.23-0.25 from index to year 3. Younger age and pre-baseline activity predicted more frequent short-term activity. Pre-baseline activity additionally predicted short-term NEDA-3 loss. Short-term findings were consistent in 3YFS patients. CDW and PIRA were rare during short-term (~ 10%) and long-term (~ 20%), even in older patients. However, during long-term, NEDA-3 loss resumed steadily and this was largely unpredictable. While cladribine showed sustained short-term efficacy, treatment response appeared more favourable in older patients and patients without pre-baseline activity. Rare CDW and PIRA events warrant more research in cladribine for disability prevention. Optimal long-term management following cladribine treatment requires more research.

title: DELPHI expert consensus-derived factors influencing the early use of monoclonal high-efficacy therapies in treatment-naïve patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To gather expert consensus regarding initiation of monoclonal high-efficacy therapies (HET) amongst treatment-naïve relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) patients in France. METHODS: The study leveraged the Delphi method to gauge consensus amongst an expert panel of 31 neurologists. Eight clinical cases with demographic, clinical and imaging characteristics were presented, prompting the experts to respond if they would recommend monoclonal HET. Additionally, potentially influential parameters were changed one at a time to assess whether the experts would recommend monoclonal HET. After a first round, an e-workshop was conducted to discuss non-consensual statements, which were re-submitted for rating (Round 2). Characteristics influencing monoclonal HET initiation were evaluated. RESULTS: 31/31 experts responded to both rounds. Consensus for or against monoclonal HET was reached for 89/108 (82.4%) statements. Factors that systematically led to monoclonal HET initiation were high brain lesion load (>20 lesions), ≥2 spinal cord lesions, ≥3 gadolinium-enhancing lesions and ≥3 infratentorial lesions. A single spinal cord lesion, in combination with other factors (which, in isolation, often but not always led to monoclonal HET), systematically led to monoclonal HET recommendation. CONCLUSION: This study suggests that the panel of French neurologists favoured monoclonal HET initiation amongst treatment-naïve RRMS patients with high radiological disease activity, whereas clinical characteristics played a complementary role.

title: Risk of Inflammatory Bowel Disease After Anti-CD20 Treatment in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Anti-CD20 biologics are widely used as disease-modifying therapy (DMT) for relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), but recent reports have raised concerns about an increased risk of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) during treatment. This study aimed to assess treatment-associated IBD risk in individuals with RRMS. OBJECTIVE: To compare the risk of new-onset IBD across different therapies for RRMS and relative to the general population. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This was a population-based cohort study conducted in Sweden. Through the Swedish MS register, initiations of rituximab, natalizumab, dimethyl fumarate, and fingolimod were identified between January 1, 2011, and December 31, 2023, in individuals with RRMS aged 18 to 55 years with at least 10 years of lookback time (5 years for dispensed drugs) and no evidence of previous IBD. These initiations were matched with general population comparator episodes selected from the Swedish population. EXPOSURES: Rituximab, comparator DMTs (natalizumab, dimethyl fumarate, fingolimod), or general population comparator. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: New-onset IBD, defined as 2 or more records on separate dates with the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, Tenth Revision, codes K50 (Crohn disease), K51 (ulcerative colitis), and/or K52.3 (indeterminate colitis). RESULTS: Among the 13 748 therapy episodes (6481 rituximab, 2976 natalizumab, 2767 dimethyl fumarate, 1524 fingolimod) in 9251 individuals (range in mean ages of the exposure groups, 35-38 years) and 61 065 matched general population episodes, 164 IBD events occurred during follow-up (40 with rituximab, 4 with comparator DMTs, and 120 in the general population). The crude incidence rate of IBD was 110 (95% CI, 76-147) per 100 000 person-years for rituximab, 13 (95% CI, 3-30) for the comparator DMTs, and 41 (95% CI, 34-48) for the general population. After adjustment for demographics and MS characteristics, the hazard ratio for the comparator DMTs vs rituximab was 0.10 (95% CI, 0.04-0.22). In the rituximab group, 62% of IBD events were classified as Crohn disease compared with 29% in the general population. The number needed to harm for rituximab vs the comparator DMTs was 131 (95% CI, 93-228) at 5 years, after full adjustment. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Results of this cohort study show that rituximab was associated with an increased risk of IBD compared with other modern MS therapies, after adjustment for differences in characteristics at therapy start. Clinicians and individuals with MS should consider IBD risk in treatment decisions and remain vigilant for gastrointestinal symptoms during anti-CD20 therapy.

title: Efficacy of Pomegranate Seed Oil (PSO) in Its Nanoformulation (GranaGard(®)) in Neurodegenerative Disease Modulation.
abstract: Oxidative stress contributes to the pathophysiology of diverse neurodegenerative diseases and acute brain injuries. Pomegranate Seed Oil (PSO) is rich in punicic acid (PA), an omega-5 fatty acid with reported antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. However, conventional PSO and standard antioxidants show limited clinical success due to poor solubility, rapid degradation, low bioavailability, and limited delivery cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). title: Subjective Sleep Quality in Relation to Relapse Status in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Propensity Score-Matched Nested Case-Control Analysis.
abstract: Background: Sleep disturbance is common in multiple sclerosis (MS), but its relationship with relapse status remains insufficiently defined. This study examined whether poorer subjective sleep quality was associated with relapse status in patients with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis. Methods: This propensity score-matched nested case-control analysis included 132 patients with relapsing-remitting MS selected from 473 consecutively evaluated patients at a tertiary multiple sclerosis centre. Patients in relapse were matched 1:1 to patients in remission by age, sex, disease duration, Expanded Disability Status Scale score, disease-modifying therapy duration and efficacy class, and relapse in the previous year. Sleep quality and related symptoms were assessed using validated questionnaires. Results: Patients in relapse were more frequently classified as poor sleepers than those in remission (59.1% vs. 36.4%; p = 0.009). In the double-adjusted logistic regression model, higher Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores were independently associated with relapse status (OR = 1.16; 95% CI 1.02-1.32; p = 0.023), whereas the remaining variables were not independently associated with relapse status. Conclusions: Poorer subjective sleep quality was independently associated with relapse status in relapsing-remitting MS, supporting sleep disturbance as a relapse-associated clinical feature rather than a proven causal risk factor.

title: A Qualitative Analysis of Focus Groups on a Community-Based Pro Bono Exercise and Lifestyle Modification Education Program for Individuals With Disability due to Multiple Sclerosis and Stroke.
abstract: The aim of this study was to identify perceived logistical, behavioral, and practical barriers to regular exercise participation in individuals with disability due to stroke and multiple sclerosis, as well as potential solutions. Focus group interviews were conducted as part of a mixed-methods prospective observational study evaluating a multi-site, pro bono, community-based exercise and lifestyle modification program. Twelve participants engaged in one of three focus groups, and data analysis was conducted using a modified grounded theory approach. Five themes were identified through thematic analysis: fear of exercising and need for safety when implementing an exercise program; personal experiences of physical and mental health and wellness; importance of social support and sense of community foster accountability and camaraderie; role of self-efficacy in daily life participation and resilience; and accessibility of fitness centers. Key factors were identified that influence exercise participation among individuals with disability due to neurological diagnosis. Overall, strong motivation to enhance overall health and wellbeing was observed; however, safety concerns and accessibility were barriers to participation. Social support and a sense of community were identified as critical factors to foster accountability and engagement. Despite existing barriers, building self-efficacy and resilience emerged as powerful enablers of long-term participation in exercise.

title: Therapeutic Multifaceted Potential of Melatonin in Neurodegenerative Diseases: From Neuroprotective Mechanisms to Translational Promise.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases, primarily characterized by progressive motor dysfunctions and debilitating memory impairments, have increasingly emerged as a major challenge in public health worldwide. The development of effective neuroprotective agents remains an urgent goal to halt the progression of neurodegenerative disorders. These agents target multiple interconnected pathological pathways, including neuroinflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, autophagy dysregulation, apoptotic cell death, pathological protein aggregation, and sustained oxidative stress. Accumulating evidence from preclinical studies suggests that melatonin, a neurohormone synthesized by the pineal gland, possesses considerable neuroprotective potential. This effect is mediated by its ability to modulate various pathophysiological processes and intracellular signaling cascades that are commonly disrupted in neurodegenerative conditions. Melatonin's pleiotropic actions, including its potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic properties, make it a promising candidate for therapeutic intervention. The present review provides a comprehensive overview of the therapeutic potential of melatonin across major neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's Disease (AD), Vascular Dementia (VD), Parkinson's Disease (PD), Multiple Sclerosis (MS), Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI), and Huntington's Disease (HD), with discussion of its roles and underlying mechanisms in each condition. Future research should prioritize well-designed clinical trials and improved formulation strategies to establish melatonin's efficacy and safety. By summarizing the current state of knowledge and identifying translational gaps, this review highlights both the therapeutic promise of melatonin and the critical steps needed to realize its potential in clinical practice.

title: Fibromyalgia, Chronic Fatigue Syndrome, and Multiple Sclerosis are associated with lower translocator protein binding affinity genotypes.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
abstract: Neuroinflammation is a known pathophysiologic mechanism in multiple sclerosis and a proposed mechanism in fibromyalgia and myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS). Positron Emission Tomography (PET) imaging of the translocator protein (TSPO) has been widely used to measure neuroinflammation, though second-generation ligands are highly sensitive to a single nucleotide polymorphism, rs6971, resulting in high, mixed, and low affinity binders. It is unknown whether this polymorphism is associated with neuroinflammatory disorders. Eighty-six total participant genotypes for TSPO binding affinity were identified through Sanger sequencing (30 fibromyalgia, 21 ME/CFS, 11 multiple sclerosis, and 24 healthy controls). Associations between patient group and genotype were assessed with Fisher's Exact test. Associations between genotype and symptom severity from self-report questionnaires were assessed with Kruskal-Wallis tests. In the present study individuals with fibromyalgia, (ME/CFS), or multiple sclerosis were more likely to have a mixed- or low-affinity genotypes compared to healthy controls. Presence of the low or mixed genotypes were also associated with greater self-reported fatigue severity and depressive symptoms. These findings should be confirmed in larger samples but suggest functional consequences of rs6971 polymorphism that may be related to the pathophysiology of pain and fatigue illnesses.

title: Comment on "Integrated determinants of multiple sclerosis susceptibility: Genetics, environment, infection and the microbiota".
Family planning in multiple sclerosis: An Australian perspective.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop evidence-based, Australia-specific recommendations for managing multiple sclerosis (MS) before conception, during pregnancy and after birth, balancing maternal health, disease control, and fetal safety. METHODS: A panel of seven Australian MS specialists, from academic and clinical backgrounds, convened (April-October 2025) via virtual meetings and email correspondence. A targeted literature review covered MS, pregnancy, postpartum relapse, breastfeeding, vaccination and disease-modifying therapy safety. Guidance from the Therapeutic Goods Administration, international clinical guidelines, and safety data were examined to inform interpretation. RESULTS: Evidence indicates that MS does not increase adverse pregnancy outcomes, although a higher risk of small-for-gestational-age birth may occur. Treatment selection should account for teratogenicity and rebound risk. Teriflunomide, fingolimod, siponimod and cladribine require cessation well before conception and are contraindicated during breastfeeding. Natalizumab can be continued until conception and through the first and second trimesters using extended-interval dosing; postpartum resumption is advised to minimise rebound relapses. Ofatumumab and ocrelizumab should be stopped if pregnancy is confirmed. Treatment decisions should be individualised through shared decision-making. European Union guidance supports use of ocrelizumab during breastfeeding, consistent with evidence of minimal monoclonal antibody transfer into breastmilk. As breastfeeding does not prevent relapse, early postpartum DMT resumption is recommended to reduce relapse risk. Contraceptive use remains low despite requirements for many therapies. CONCLUSION: With proactive planning, women with MS can achieve optimal pregnancy outcomes. This consensus integrates evidence, regulatory considerations and Australian guidance to support a practical framework for family planning in MS.

title: The reported pain-cognition dissociation in multiple sclerosis: different pain scores for objective and perceived cognition.
Body Composition Findings During Weight Loss Observed in Fingolimod-Treated Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Fingolimod is a sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulator widely used in the treatment of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS). Clinically significant weight loss during fingolimod therapy has rarely been characterized in detail, particularly regarding body composition findings and the relative contribution of adipose tissue loss. We report a 54-year-old man with RRMS who developed progressive, unintentional weight loss during fingolimod therapy. Over ∼2 years, body weight decreased from 100 to 78 kg without appetite loss, dietary restriction, increased physical activity, or major lifestyle changes. Extensive multidisciplinary evaluation did not identify malignancy, chronic infection, gastrointestinal disease, endocrine abnormalities, or systemic inflammatory disorders. Multifrequency bioelectrical impedance analysis demonstrated low adipose tissue parameters with relative preservation of skeletal muscle mass and hydration status, suggesting that adipose tissue reduction represented a major component of the observed weight loss pattern. Body weight subsequently remained stable during additional clinical follow-up. This case describes progressive unintentional weight loss during fingolimod therapy in a patient with RRMS, with body composition findings suggesting predominant adipose tissue involvement. Although causality cannot be established from a single observation, the temporal association and exclusion of major alternative etiologies suggest a possible association that may merit further investigation. This report also highlights the potential value of body composition assessment in patients presenting with unexplained weight loss during fingolimod therapy.

title: Ceruloplasmin in Disorders of the Nervous System.
abstract: Ceruloplasmin (Cp) is a multicopper ferroxidase that links copper handling, iron export, and redox homeostasis. Within the nervous system, these functions are critical because disruption of iron and copper balance can amplify oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neuronal vulnerability. Although Cp has long been studied as a circulating biomarker, most reports characterize it only by protein concentration, leaving its enzymatic and structural status comparatively unexplored. Here, we synthesize human literature on Cp across major neurological disorders, with attention to studies that assess Cp's ferroxidase activity, oxidation, fragmentation, and copper-binding state alongside its circulating levels. The evidence is by far most extensive in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases, which together account for the majority of the reviewed literature: reduced ferroxidase activity, increased Cp oxidation, and altered non-Cp-bound copper are repeatedly linked to disease severity, regional iron accumulation, and biomarker-defined patient subgroups; in several studies, these alterations were independent of total Cp concentration. A smaller but growing body of evidence in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, multiple sclerosis, essential tremor, and the cerebellar ataxias points to a related pattern of Cp-linked iron mishandling contributing to neuronal vulnerability. Preliminary findings from a few small studies in schizophrenia and a single study in obsessive-compulsive disorder further suggest that circulating Cp levels track systemic inflammatory and oxidative states in these conditions. From these investigations, a picture emerges where Cp's functional and structural integrity, rather than its abundance alone, is the more informative correlate of disease-relevant metal dyshomeostasis, most clearly demonstrated in Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases. Based on this body of work, we propose that future studies adopt combined assessments of Cp quantity and function to clarify disease-specific Cp signatures and to evaluate whether correcting Cp activity or copper/iron imbalance can improve outcomes.

title: Salivary Proteomics Reveals Disease- and Therapy-Associated Molecular Patterns in Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic immune-mediated disease for which non-invasive biomarkers, able to detect disease- and treatment-associated molecular changes, are needed. We characterized the whole-saliva proteome of patients with relapsing-remitting (RR) MS at baseline before treatment initiation (MS-T0; n = 66) and after six months of disease-modifying therapy (MS-T1; n = 40), in comparison with healthy controls (HC; n = 31). Nano-liquid chromatography-high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry identified 1305 proteins, of which 209 differed among the main comparisons. Pairwise and paired analyses distinguished persistent RRMS-associated alterations, baseline-attenuation patterns with changes shifting towards HC levels, treatment-associated differences emerging at MS-T1, and longitudinal-only alterations. The identified patterns are descriptive and cannot be interpreted as evidence of pharmacological treatment effects or clinical response. The existence of specific RRMS alterations was supported by exploratory Random Forest, which classified HC, MS-T0 and MS-T1 samples using a panel of 50 proteins, most of which (96%) also showed significant changes in univariate tests. Reactome enrichment evidenced that proteins pertaining to the identified patterns are mainly involved in innate immunity, neutrophil degranulation, cell-death pathways, cytokine signalling, and protein folding. These findings indicate that six months of therapy was associated with substantial salivary proteome changes and support saliva as a candidate biofluid for longitudinal molecular monitoring and non-invasive detection of treatment-associated salivary proteome variations in RRMS.

title: Brain-Computer Interfaces for Cognitive Rehabilitation: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Cognitive diseases/disorders are a major cause of disability affecting millions of people worldwide due to pathologies or conditions such as Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, vascular cognitive impairment, and attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder. The effects of these diseases/disorders can range from subjective cognitive complaints to mild cognitive impairment and even dementia that can affect multiple cognitive domains, causing disability and alterations in daily functioning and quality of life. Cognitive training has been researched as a potential therapeutic option for treating cognitive disability. In particular, cognitive training delivered using brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) represents a promising technology for cognitive rehabilitation. For this reason, this work presents a narrative review aimed at bridging the clinical aspects of cognition performance and the technical features of BCI systems. Additionally, it reports on the current advances of BCIs for cognitive rehabilitation in the pathologies/conditions that are the main contributors of cognitive impairment globally. Specifically, Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, mild cognitive impairment, cerebrovascular diseases, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder were included in the review; other pathologies that can also cause cognitive impairment such as multiple sclerosis, traumatic brain injury, brain tumors, infectious diseases, and psychiatric conditions such as schizophrenia or autism spectrum disorder, or drug or toxin-related causes were outside the scope of the present review. Across the literature, studies have reported that BCI cognitive training can improve cognition performance for mild cognitive impairment, stroke, and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, showcasing its feasibility as a complementary therapy. However, the amount of evidence is still scarce, with few reported randomized controlled clinical trials and all of the applications comprising non-invasive systems using electroencephalography, while invasive or other non-invasive approaches remain largely unassessed. Therefore, further research regarding the design of BCIs for targeting specific cognitive domains is necessary to allow for the future introduction of these types of systems into clinical rehabilitation environments, rather than only demonstrating their feasibility, as has been mainly done to date.

title: Impact of newly diagnosed multiple sclerosis on marital status and partner relationship.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence on short-term impact of multiple sclerosis (MS) diagnosis on intimate relationships remains limited. This study investigated the perceived impact of MS diagnosis on relationship status within the first year following diagnosis. METHODS: This survey-based observational study used data from the Swiss Multiple Sclerosis Registry (SMSR). Factors potentially associated with perceived MS direct impact on relationship status within the first year after diagnosis were explored using logistic regression. Among participants reporting that MS impacted their relationship, we explored changes in relationship status and factors associated with relationship dissolution. RESULTS: Among 881 participants included (74% female), 453 were married, 235 with a partner, and 193 single at diagnosis. Overall, 89 participants (10.1%) reported that MS diagnosis impacted their relationship (i.e., 6.2% of married; 14.5% of partnered; 14% of single). Compared with married participants, partnered (ORadj 2.3; 95%CI 1.30-4.06) and single participants (ORadj 2.26; 95%CI 1.25-4.07) were more likely to report impact. Cognitive symptoms were associated with higher odds of reporting impact (ORadj 2.02, 95%CI 1.28-3.19). Among married participants, primary progressive MS was associated with increased odds of relationship impact (ORadj 3.21; 95%CI 1.15-8.33). Among partnered participants, men were more likely than women to report an impacted relationship (ORadj 3.00; 95%CI 1.23-7.25). Among participants with reported relationship impact, relationship trajectories included continuation, strengthening, and dissolution. None of the studied factors were associated with relationship dissolution. CONCLUSION: One in ten participants reported MS diagnosis impacting their relationship, and consequent relationship changes were heterogeneous, suggesting that this influence may belong to broader psychosocial processes.

title: Real-world treatment in pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis: Data from the Swiss pediatric inflammatory brain disease cohort study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pediatric-onset multiple sclerosis (POMS) exhibits more aggressive inflammation than adult-onset multiple sclerosis, with higher relapse rates, faster lesion accrual, earlier disability progression, and a greater risk of cognitive impairment. Appropriate treatment is crucial to minimize lifelong impairment. METHODS: This multicenter, observational cohort study examined patients from the Swiss Pediatric Inflammatory Brain Disease Registry with POMS who received index treatment with disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) of varying efficacy: mild-efficacy therapy (MET), intermediate-efficacy therapy (IET), and high-efficacy therapy (HET). We analyzed demographic and baseline characteristics, index treatment type, reasons for switching, breakthrough disease activity, and pre- and post-treatment annualized relapse rates before and after index treatment start. We further studied index treatment prescription development over time. Descriptive statistics were used. RESULTS: Of 41 patients with POMS, 32 (78%) were female. Thirty-nine received disease-modifying treatment post-diagnosis: 15 started MET, 13 IET, and 11 HET. Discontinuation was highest with MET (67%), followed by IET (54%), and HET (18%). Side effects prompted switching in the MET group, while disease activity drove switching in IET and HET groups. Mean annualized relapse rates decreased after index treatment from 1.07 to 0.43 with MET, from 1.17 to 0.33 with IET, and from 1.73 to 0.09 with HET. After 2019, MET was discontinued as index treatment. DISCUSSION: POMS treatment has evolved; since 2019, only IET and HET have been used in this Swiss cohort, achieving ARR reductions and lower discontinuation rates compared to MET.

title: Exercise-induced pain modulation in multiple sclerosis: Why pain phenotype matters.
Identification of BRD4 as a Shared Diagnostic Biomarker Between Bipolar Disorder and Multiple Sclerosis Using Machine Learning.
abstract: Bipolar disorder (BD) is closely associated with multiple sclerosis (MS), but their shared molecular mechanisms and specific diagnostic biomarkers remain unclear. This study integrated microarray expression profiling and machine learning to identify shared core genes and underlying mechanisms between BD and MS. Gene expression datasets and peripheral-blood transcriptome datasets were obtained from the GEO database. After per-cohort quantile normalization, shared genes were identified by differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. A protein-protein interaction network was constructed, and key genes were screened using the MCODE plugin. Three machine learning algorithms were combined to identify the final core gene. A total of 229 shared genes were initially obtained and further filtered to 55 key genes.

title: Hidden Markov Modeling Reveals Altered Functional Network Dynamics in Multiple Sclerosis.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a neurodegenerative and demyelinating disease of the central nervous system. Recent evidence suggests that localized gray matter atrophy in MS may be involved in distributed functional brain networks. However, the dynamic trajectory of functional network alterations in MS remains unclear. The current study extends prior network-mediated findings and aims to investigate the dynamic functional connectivity (dFC) and energetic landscape across an atrophy-prone network in MS. Twenty MS participants and twenty healthy controls (HC) underwent resting-state fMRI. The atrophy-based functional network (AFN) model was implemented, and time series from atrophy-prone regions were fit to a 12-state hidden Markov model. Each functional network state, a recurring pattern of activity across the AFN, was characterized by the AFN regions with the strongest activation. The states were then grouped into two metastates. Dynamic functional network metrics were compared between groups by permutation testing and correlated with disability and cognition. The energetic landscape of the network was mapped with a pairwise maximum-entropy model. Temporal irreversibility was also measured, which defines the arrow-of-time asymmetry of network dynamics. People with MS showed lower occupancy of state 1, which peaked on the right middle frontal and anterior cingulate cortex. Occupancy and mean lifetime were higher in states 3 and 10 (p < 0.05). In state 3, cortical activity was below the network average, and state 10 peaked on the postcentral gyrus. At the metastate level, MS participants spent more time in metastate M1 and less in M2 (p = 0.04). Within the MS group, a longer interval between visits to state 3 was associated with greater disability (r = 0.57), and a higher switching rate in state 10 with poorer verbal fluency (r = -0.50). The energetic landscape was similar between groups. Temporal irreversibility was lower in MS, mainly across subcortical connections. MS participants dwelled longer in specific dFC states of the AFN, while the rate of transition between states did not differ from healthy controls. Dynamic functional network metrics were associated with disability and cognitive performance and may serve as functional correlates of clinical impairment. The states were similar between groups, whereas the directed drive between states was lower across subcortical connections. This pattern suggests altered network dynamics rather than altered network architecture in MS. Findings from this study characterize the functional network dynamics of neurodegeneration in MS, which may inform future development of network-based approaches for monitoring disease progression.

title: Perceived Acceptability, Design Preferences, and User Requirements for a Proposed Ear-Worn Device for Heart-Rate and Ear-Temperature Monitoring with Localized Neck Cooling: A Pre-Prototype Mixed-Methods Study in People with Multiple Sclerosis.

Association Between Local Ascending Aortic Elastic Properties and Left Ventricular Global Longitudinal Strain in Patients with Multiple Sclerosis: A Cross-Sectional Case-Control Echocardiographic Study.
From Global Evidence to Saudi Practice: A Structured Evidence Map of the Diagnosis, Molecular Targets, and Therapeutic Strategies of Multiple Sclerosis in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) has shifted in a generation from an uncommon diagnosis in Saudi Arabia to a major cause of neurological disability in young adults. Available Saudi data describe clinical characteristics broadly similar to those reported elsewhere in the Middle East and do not show that Saudi patients differ from trial populations, although this does not establish equivalent efficacy or safety. How far global advances are usable in the Kingdom has not, however, been synthesized. This narrative review maps diagnostic and therapeutic strategies across five separately reported domains (clinical evidence, 2022 national consensus listing, affordability, monitoring requirement, regional data), with categories assigned by a pre-specified rule, not a composite grade. Regional evidence on established therapies is entirely observational: cohorts report favourable outcomes with fingolimod, natalizumab, and off-label rituximab but cannot establish comparative effectiveness, and physicians report cost, availability, and insurance formularies as constraints whose extent has not been quantified. Diagnosis, now based on the 2024 McDonald revision, is transferable in knowledge but depends on AQP4-IgG testing, MRI, and biomarker capacity whose national distribution is undocumented, with neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder an important differential. Tolebrutinib, recently approved in Europe for non-relapsing secondary progressive MS, and experimental modalities remain regulatory or research questions without regional data. Saudi studies document substantial payer costs of disease-modifying therapy, but none have measured how often cost or infrastructure alters treatment; we propose a prioritized research agenda.

title: DNA donation decisions, uncertainty, and perceived learning in a Serbian survey on multiple sclerosis genetics.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine willingness to donate DNA for multiple sclerosis (MS) research, with particular attention to uncertainty versus unwillingness, and perceived learning during completion of a questionnaire on MS genetics. METHODS: An online cross-sectional survey was conducted in Serbia. Regression analyses focused on the non-professional subsample. Multinomial logistic regression examined willing, unwilling, and insufficient-information responses to DNA donation, while multivariable linear regression examined perceived learning, measured by "I know now" responses to seven informational items. RESULTS: Among 1075 valid DNA-donation responses, 49.8% were willing, 22.9% lacked sufficient information to decide, and 27.3% were unwilling. In adjusted analyses, not wanting personal genetic risk information was more strongly associated with unwillingness than with uncertainty, while prior awareness of genetic data protection was associated with less uncertainty relative to both willingness and unwillingness. Respondents reported a median perceived-learning score of 5 out of 7. Greater objective knowledge and familiarity with MS were associated with higher perceived-learning scores, whereas male sex and age ≤ 20 years were associated with lower scores. CONCLUSION: Respondents who lacked sufficient information to decide about DNA donation differed from those who were unwilling to participate, supporting the treatment of uncertainty as a distinct response. The reported perceived learning also suggests that questionnaires incorporating informational content may provide an opportunity to support awareness alongside data collection. PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: Research communication should distinguish insufficient information from refusal and clearly address personal genetic risk information and data protection. Informational questionnaires may complement these efforts, although their educational effects require objective evaluation.

title: Depressive symptoms and CSF markers of B-cell activation in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Psychiatric symptoms in people with multiple sclerosis (pwMS) may be considered as a biologically driven manifestation of the disease. B-cell activation is reliably reflected in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) by means of oligoclonal bands (OCBs) and the kappa free light chain (κ-FLC) index. We retrospectively explored the relationship of CSF OCBs and κ-FLC index with psychiatric symptoms in a consecutive series of newly diagnosed pwMS. Both OCB positivity and a κ-FLC index ≥3.3 were significantly associated with higher depressive symptoms scores. Multivariate analyses confirmed the association for OCB positivity and a borderline association for a κ-FLC index ≥3.3. Our findings support the need to systematically assess psychiatric symptoms in MS as a biologically based component of the disease.

title: Effects of Occupational Therapy Interventions on Occupational Performance and Physical and Cognitive Fatigue in Adults with Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
Age-Stratified Comparison of Gait Biomechanics in People with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis and Healthy Individuals: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
journal: Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology
abstract: Background and Objectives: Gait impairment is a common and disabling manifestation of multiple sclerosis, affecting mobility, independence, and quality of life. However, gait differences between people with multiple sclerosis and healthy individuals have not been well characterized within corresponding age strata. Methods: This exploratory cross-sectional study included 23 participants with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis and 50 healthy individuals aged 20-69 years. Participants underwent instrumented gait analysis at self-selected walking speed using a Vicon motion-capture system synchronized with force plates. Spatiotemporal parameters, lower-limb and pelvic kinematics, and ground reaction forces were assessed. Between-group comparisons were performed within predefined age strata (20-39, 40-49, 50-59, and 60-69 years) using one-dimensional Statistical Parametric Mapping and non-parametric analyses. Results: Across age strata, participants with relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis generally showed slower walking and shorter stride-related measures, together with phase-specific multi-joint kinematic and ground reaction force deviations. Estimated gait-speed and stride-length differences were largest in the youngest stratum, whereas mean stride width was 0.04 m greater in both the youngest and oldest strata; however, confidence intervals were wide, and no between-stratum contrast was tested. Exploratory threshold crossings were not interpreted as evidence that the underlying effects differed among strata. Conclusions: The age-stratified, participant-level analysis identified recurrent differences in forward progression, lower-limb and pelvic kinematics, and loading and propulsion. These findings provide a quantitative description that may support individualized gait assessment and hypothesis generation for adequately powered studies. They do not establish an independent effect of age or an age-by-disease interaction.

title: Short term effect of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation of the medial sensorimotor cortex for neurogenic pelvic floor dysfunction in multiple sclerosis: a randomized, double blind, sham controlled trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Neurogenic pelvic floor dysfunction, comprising bladder, bowel and sexual disturbance, affects most people with multiple sclerosis (MS) and responds poorly to pharmacotherapy. The medial sensorimotor cortex contains the pelvic floor representation, but controlled evidence for cortical neuromodulation in MS is scarce and bladder focused. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the short term efficacy and safety of inhibitory (1 Hz) repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the vertex (Cz) in MS-related pelvic floor dysfunction. METHODS: Forty-five patients with definite MS (Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) ≤6.0) and actionable bladder symptoms Screening Tool (ABSST≥8) were randomized 2:1 in a double-blind, sham-controlled single centre trial to active (n = 30) or sham (n = 15) stimulation: 1 Hz rTMS at 90-100% resting motor threshold (900 pulses) over Cz across 10 weekday sessions; sham used a 90° tilted coil with synchronized scalp electrodes. ABSST, Neurogenic Bowel Dysfunction (NBD) score, Multiple Sclerosis Impact Scale 29(MSIS-29), Multiple Sclerosis Intimacy and Sexuality Questionnaire (MSISQ- 19), Overactive Bladder Questionnaire-Short Form (OAB -q SF) were assessed at baseline and 12 weeks post treatment. RESULTS: ABSST fell from 18.6 ± 4.5 to 13.9 ± 5.1 with active stimulation versus 17.8 ± 3.8 to 17.1 ± 3.5 with sham (ANCOVA adjusted difference -3.98, 95%CI -6.75 to -1.22; standardized effect -0.93; p = 0.006). After baseline and multiplicity adjustment, benefit persisted for bowel (NBD; FDR adjusted p = 0.004) and sexual (MSISQ-19; p = 0.036) domains, but not OAB-q SF or MSIS-29. Bladder improvement correlated with bowel (r = 0.464) and sexual (r = 0.374) improvement. No serious adverse events occurred. All 45 participants completed all ten sessions and the 12 week assessment. CONCLUSIONS: Inhibitory vertex rTMS produced sustained, coherent cross domain improvement in MS-related pelvic floor dysfunction exceeding sham, consistent with modulation of a shared central substrate and supports cortical neuromodulation as a promising, well tolerated adjunct.

title: Autoimmune comorbidity profiles in MOGAD and AQP4-NMOSD: a real-world evidence study of top 10 autoimmune disorders across the pre- and post-COVID-19 eras.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) and aquaporin-4 antibody-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (AQP4-NMOSD) are antibody-mediated demyelinating disorders presenting with distinct immunopathogenic mechanisms. Systemic autoimmune comorbidity patterns and their evolution across the COVID-19 era remain incompletely characterized in real-world settings. We compared systemic autoimmune burdens and immune laboratory profiles between MOGAD and AQP4-NMOSD, systematically evaluating temporal changes before and after the COVID-19 pandemic. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX Global Research Network (2015-2025). Antibody-confirmed cohorts included 2533 MOGAD and 453 AQP4-NMOSD patients (multiple sclerosis was strictly excluded). Ten systemic autoimmune categories were identified using ICD-10 codes. Immune laboratory markers, including antinuclear antibodies, anti-dsDNA, complement levels, and immunoglobulin dynamics, were analyzed. Temporal analyses included pre-/post-diagnosis windows and pre-/post-COVID-19 era stratification. RESULTS: AQP4-NMOSD patients were older and predominantly female compared to those with MOGAD. AQP4-NMOSD demonstrated a substantially higher baseline systemic autoimmune burden, including systemic lupus erythematosus (16%vs 1%), other connective tissue involvement (12%vs 5%), rheumatoid arthritis (6%vs 2%), and autoimmune gastrointestinal disease. Marked serum IgG reduction and post-diagnosis autoantibody titer resolution occurred predominantly in AQP4-NMOSD. COVID-era comparisons revealed persistent, high comorbidity odds in AQP4-NMOSD alongside selective temporal accrual of connective tissue, vascular, and thyroid comorbidities within MOGAD. CONCLUSION: AQP4-NMOSD is embedded within a broader humoral autoimmune network, whereas MOGAD exhibits a restricted systemic immune phenotype. The COVID-19 era accentuated preexisting subtype-specific architectures rather than uniformly increasing autoimmune burden. These findings support subtype-specific autoimmune surveillance strategies and reinforce precision phenotyping in antibody-mediated demyelinating disorders.

title: Ethmoid bone marrow region modulates lymphoid activation and differentiation with distinct myeloid profile in neuroinflammation.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: The skull bone marrow axis has recently emerged as an important source of immune cells during neuroinflammation, including in the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), the mouse model of multiple sclerosis. The cribriform plate bone marrow (cpBM), is a portion of the ethmoid bone of the skull of mice, and is positioned next to nasal regions. At the cribriform plate olfactory nerves pass through the skull and recent evidence supports that it represents an important immune niche with links to CSF outflow and connections to cpBM. Previous data supports cellular composition of the ethmoid bone marrow in mice is altered in neuroinflammation suggesting it senses inflammatory cues, but the exact nature of these changes is still unclear. Here using scRNAseq and flow cytometry of the ethmoid bone marrow region we test how the region responds to EAE. In addition, we also compare the cpBM region with systemic bone marrow in the femur to understand region specific differences. We report that neuroinflammation creates a regulatory response at these sites and implicates the cpBM in controlling these effects. A better understanding of the cribriform niche may offer new treatments for neuroinflammatory disease.

title: MRI before CSF: prospective evidence that the 2024 McDonald criteria reduce lumbar punctures.
abstract: The 2024 McDonald criteria for the diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS) introduced MRI biomarkers including the central vein sign (CVS), which may substitute for cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) testing in certain circumstances. We evaluated how the sequential application of MRI biomarkers incorporated into the 2024 criteria changes the need for CSF examination. Our primary analysis used the DECISIve cohort, a prospective, multicentre study of patients with typical clinically isolated syndrome who all required lumbar puncture (LP) for diagnosis under 2017 MS diagnostic criteria. Participants received both LP and MRI with T2* susceptibility-based imaging. We applied the 2024 criteria sequentially, evaluating MRI topographies and CVS status prior to determining whether LP was still required. To assess generalisability, we evaluated a separate consecutive single-centre real-world cohort. In DECISIve (n=98), 70% (69/98) could be diagnosed without LP under 2024 criteria when MRI with CVS analysis was performed first: 21% (21/98) had lesions in ≥4 topographies, 72% (48/67) with 2-3 topographies were CVS-positive. In the real-world cohort (n=87), 69% (60/87) met the 2024 criteria without LP, consistent with the trial finding. There was significant concordance between paraclinical tests in DECISIve: 90% (19/21) of participants with ≥4 topographies were also CVS-positive, and 81% (56/69) of OCB-positive participants were CVS-positive. Only 11% (10/88) of participants with at least two topographies were solely OCB-positive. Assessing MRI with CVS first removes the need for LP in most patients, a finding corroborated in real-world practice. Collaborative effort is needed to develop CVS/PRL expertise across centres.

title: Limited Gut Microbiome Differences Between Relapsing-Remitting and Secondary Progressive Multiple Sclerosis: A Shotgun Metagenomic Study.
abstract: The gut microbiome may contribute to multiple sclerosis (MS) pathophysiology, but its relationship with disease phenotype and progression remains unclear. To characterize taxonomic and functional gut microbiome differences between relapsing-remitting MS (RRMS) and secondary progressive MS (SPMS) and their associations with neurological disability and circulating biomarkers. This cross-sectional study included 89 participants (30 healthy controls, 29 RRMS, and 30 SPMS). Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was used to assess microbial diversity, taxonomic profiles, and predefined short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-related pathways, integrated with disability measures and serum GFAP, NfL, and S100B. SPMS participants were substantially older than those with RRMS (median 49.0 vs. 31.0 years), prompting age-adjusted analyses and an age-overlap sensitivity analysis. Alpha diversity and overall microbial community composition were similar across groups. SPMS showed greater interindividual microbial community dispersion than RRMS in the full cohort, with a similar direction and magnitude but attenuated statistical significance in the age-overlap sensitivity analysis. Exploratory taxonomic signals were not confirmed by FDR-controlled analyses. No robust phenotype-specific differences in predicted SCFA-related pathways or associations of taxonomic or functional features with disability or circulating biomarkers were identified. Greater microbial community dispersion in SPMS was observed in the full cohort, but this finding was attenuated in the age-overlap sensitivity analysis and should be considered preliminary. Overall, these findings do not support a distinct SPMS-associated gut microbiome signature, although potential phenotype-related differences cannot be excluded.

title: Baclofen for Spasticity in Multiple Sclerosis: A Comprehensive Narrative Review.
abstract: Baclofen, a GABA-B receptor agonist developed as an anticonvulsant in the 1960s and repurposed for spasticity in the 1970s, is recommended as a first-line oral treatment for spasticity in multiple sclerosis (MS) by UK NICE guidance and is used similarly, though not necessarily designated identically, in many other jurisdictions. It acts at two sites within the spinal stretch reflex arc: presynaptically on Ia afferent terminals in the dorsal horn, where it reduces excitatory neurotransmitter release, and postsynaptically on ventral horn interneurons and α-motoneurons, where it hyperpolarises the cell and suppresses firing. Only a small fraction of an oral dose crosses the blood-CNS barrier, so oral dosing requires high systemic doses that cause sedation, ataxia and CNS depression. Intrathecal delivery bypasses the barrier, allowing a much lower dose and fewer brain-mediated side effects. Other drawbacks include a short, variable half-life, GABA-B receptor downregulation contributing to adverse effects and intrathecal tolerance, and withdrawal that has proved fatal. The narrow efficacy-to-side-effect margin is probably intrinsic to GABA-B receptor activation. This narrative review covers baclofen's neuroanatomy, pharmacokinetics, administration routes, efficacy, comparators, long-term outcomes, interactions, special populations, and regulatory history. Long-term follow-up shows durable control without worsening sedation, but the one study using validated quality-of-life measures found no significant improvement despite clear spasticity reduction. Weighing benefit against harm, this review concludes that baclofen offers a net benefit, but conditionally: only for carefully selected, individually titrated, and actively monitored patients. Because this is a narrative rather than systematic review, source selection was not governed by a prespecified protocol, some clinical estimates rely on secondary or aggregate data, and the underlying literature is heterogeneous in design and quality.

title: A Comparative Review and Benchmarking Evaluation of Step Detection Methods for Longitudinal Gait Assessment.
abstract: Gait analysis based on inertial measurement units (IMUs) enables scalable longitudinal gait assessment, with step detection as a foundational component. However, an understanding of available step detection methods and their comparative performance across sensor placements, clinical populations, and real-world environments remains limited. This paper addresses this gap through a twofold contribution. First, a structured taxonomic review organises the landscape into six families-rule-based heuristics, phase portrait, template matching, time-frequency analysis, adaptive oscillators, and machine learning-characterising the trade-offs of each in terms of noise robustness, generalisability, and computational efficiency. Second, nine algorithms drawn from five of these families, all but phase portrait, are benchmarked across three large datasets encompassing healthy adults and people with mobility-impairing conditions such as Parkinson's disease and multiple sclerosis, at multiple sensor placements under both controlled laboratory and free-living conditions. Accuracy depended on sensor placement, gait pathology and recording environment: step detection proved reliable in structured laboratory settings across most sensor locations and clinical cohorts, whereas unsupervised free-living monitoring produced a substantial degradation for most algorithms. Over all conditions, the three evaluated time-frequency methods obtained the best average ranks for detection accuracy, step-duration error and cadence error.

title: True Versus Sham Thread Embedding Acupuncture for Spasticity-Related Symptoms and Disabilities in Multiple Sclerosis: Study Protocol of a Randomized Controlled Trial.
Neuro-JEPA: Building and Evaluating Health-System Scale Neuroimaging Foundation Models with Mixture of Experts.
abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain routinely combines complementary contrasts-including T1-weighted (T1w), T2-weighted (T2w) and FLAIR sequences-to capture anatomy and pathology. Although foundation models trained on large neuroimaging datasets have shown promise, it remains unclear whether they effectively integrate these complementary contrasts across diverse clinical settings. Here we present Neuro-JEPA, a multimodal foundation model that learns unified representations across structural brain MRIs. Neuro-JEPA combines latent predictive learning with a sparse Mixture-of-Experts architecture to encode multiple MRI contrasts within a single model. The model is pretrained on 1.55 million scans from 428,647 clinical imaging studies spanning T1w, T2w and FLAIR sequences. The model performance is evaluated on 47 downstream tasks across three independent health systems and 12 public datasets, encompassing single-contrast, multimodal and cross-domain applications. Across these evaluations, Neuro-JEPA achieved the strongest overall performance and generalized robustly across heterogeneous cohorts, outperforming existing neuroimaging foundation models and strong conventional baselines in the majority of comparisons despite using less than one-third of the pretraining data of leading models. Performance gains were particularly pronounced in data-scarce settings, reaching up to 15% over prior foundation models for clinically important pathologies including gliosis and multiple sclerosis. Neuro-JEPA showed clinically relevant capabilities across domains, including prediction of amyloid status and progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's disease dementia, stroke identification and classification, and prediction of post-stroke functional outcome and length of stay. Together, these results show that data scale, curation and principled model design can act synergistically to produce broadly transferable neuroimaging representations, and establish Neuro-JEPA as a scalable framework toward general-purpose multimodal foundation models for neurological imaging.

title: Deep Learning-Based Multiple Sclerosis Lesion Segmentation at 7 Tesla: Comparison of Single- and Multi-Contrast MRI Inputs.
abstract: Automated lesion segmentation can support rapid and reproducible quantitative assessment and long-term monitoring of multiple sclerosis. Ultra-high-field 7T MRI provides increased spatial resolution and lesion visibility but introduces challenges for automated analysis, including field inhomogeneity, susceptibility-related artifacts, and spatially varying image contrast. Although deep learning methods perform well at conventional field strengths, their application to 7T MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated nnUNet using FLAIR alone, MP2RAGE alone, and combined MP2RAGE+FLAIR. The dataset included 115 longitudinal 7T MRI scans from 57 patients with MS, with 20 scans from 11 independent patients reserved for testing. DeepMedic was included as a comparative architecture. On the test set, nnUNet achieved mean DSC values of 0.72, 0.71, and 0.66 for combined, MP2RAGE-only, and FLAIR-only inputs, respectively. No significant DSC differences were observed between nnUNet and DeepMedic. For both architectures, adding FLAIR to MP2RAGE did not show a statistically significant additional benefit in the present test cohort, whereas MP2RAGE-containing inputs significantly outperformed FLAIR-only input. The findings of the present study provide preliminary evidence suggesting that the observed voxel-level segmentation performance was primarily associated with the inclusion of MP2RAGE. However, lesion-level performance depended on lesion size, indicating further investigation of contrast-specific effects on small-lesion detection.

title: Hypertension in People with Multiple Sclerosis: Epidemiology, Mechanisms, Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy, and Clinical Implications.
abstract: Hypertension is a major cardiovascular risk factor, but its epidemiology in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS) remains unclear. Whether PwMS have a higher prevalence of hypertension than the general population, the potential pathways linking the two conditions, and the association between hypertension and MS-related outcomes remain incompletely understood. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on the prevalence of hypertension in PwMS, examines potential immunological, autonomic, vascular, behavioral, and treatment-related pathways that may link MS and hypertension, and explores how MS disease-modifying therapies may influence blood pressure regulation. It also reviews evidence on the association between hypertension and neurological disability, mobility, cognitive function, visual outcomes, and markers of neurodegeneration in PwMS, as well as hypertensive disorders of pregnancy in women with MS. Finally, it discusses the clinical implications of these findings and identifies priorities for future research.

title: Enkephalin Treatment Reduces Elevated Brain Glia in Mice With Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic, autoimmune disorder that culminates in severe motor and cognitive deficits. The progression of the disease is associated with inflammation and demyelination of the brain and spinal cord. Activation and proliferation of glia, including astrocytes and oligodendrocytes, in the brain are hallmarks. Persons with MS (PwMS) have significantly low levels of the neuropeptide [Met Female C57BL/6J mice were inoculated with myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (MOG The number of reactive astroglia in EAE brains was elevated relative to the number in normal mouse brains. Daily treatment with OGF/Met-Enk reduced GFAP-positive cells in all 3 brain regions, and LDN reduced astrocyte number in the corpus callosum and subventricular zone. Astrocytes in treated EAE mice had process lengths that were comparable with those in normal mice, suggesting less reactivity. The numbers of oligodendrocytes in the corpus callosum of EAE+LDN mice were significantly reduced relative to EAE+PBS tissues. These results demonstrate quantitative changes in reactive glia in EAE mouse brains following treatment with OGF/Met-Enk and LDN and corroborate other studies showing that OGF/Met-Enk and LDN treatment increase plasma enkephalins, reduce inflammation and decrease pro-inflammatory cytokines.

title: Effects of blood flow restriction therapy on lower-limb strength in multiple sclerosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurodegenerative disease that impairs muscle strength, gait, and functional capacity. Blood flow restriction (BFR) therapy has emerged as a promising low-load rehabilitation strategy, although evidence in people with MS (pwMS) remains limited and heterogeneous. To analyze the current scientific evidence regarding the effects of BFR therapy on lower-limb muscle strength in pwMS. PRISMA-based review included a systematic search of eight electronic databases. Clinical and quasi-experimental studies involving people with MS that evaluated lower-limb BFR interventions were included, with lower-limb muscle strength as the primary outcome. The primary outcome for meta-analysis was de standardized mean differences (SMD) in strength. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using the PEDro, JBI scales, RoB 2 and ROBINS-I V2 tools. Five studies met the inclusion criteria. Interventions ranged from 6 to 12 weeks with low training loads (30-40% of one-repetition maximum) and occlusion pressures ranging from 30% to 80% of arterial occlusion pressure. Compared with exercise alone, exercise combined with BFR significantly improved quadriceps (SMD=-0.55) and hamstring strength (SMD=-0.38), and possibly reduced fatigue (SMD=-0.35), with low heterogeneity across analyses. However, the statistical significance of the effect on quadriceps strength was lost in the sensitivity analysis. Methodological quality and overall risk of bias varied from moderate to good. BFR therapy may improve lower-limb strength (more consistently for hamstrings than quadriceps) and may reduce fatigue in people with MS compared with exercise alone, but the certainty of the evidence is low. The quadriceps effect was not robust to sensitivity analysis, and no clear benefit was found for sit-to-stand or gait outcomes. The evidence does not allow conclusions on equivalence to high-load training or on optimal occlusion pressure or intervention duration. Lager, high-quality randomized trials are needed.

title: Examining the effectiveness of theory-based nursing interventions for patients with multiple sclerosis (MS): A systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this systematic review was to evaluate the effectiveness of theory-based nursing interventions for individuals with multiple sclerosis (MS). METHODS: A comprehensive search of the PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Web of Science, MEDLINE, and Cochrane databases was performed to identify randomized controlled trials (RCTs) published between January 1, 2015, and May 1, 2025. Following a rigorous screening process in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines, nine studies meeting the predefined eligibility criteria were included in the review. RESULTS: The included studies evaluated interventions grounded in nursing theories, including Orem's Self-Care Model (n = 3), the Continuous Care Model (n = 3), Pender's Health Promotion Model (n = 1), the Theory of Goal Attainment (n = 1), and the Collaborative Care Model (n = 1). The findings indicate that the application of these theory-based nursing interventions were associated with statistically significant improvements across multiple outcomes, including quality of life, self-efficacy, activities of daily living, treatment adherence, hope, fatigue, stress regulation, lifestyle modification, and sleep quality. Most studies exhibited high methodological quality. CONCLUSION: Theory-based nursing interventions not only yield significant positive effects on physical, psychological, and behavioral outcomes among individuals with multiple sclerosis but also serve as an essential framework for guiding the planning and delivery of holistic nursing care.

title: A large, comprehensive labeled MRI dataset of the human lateral ventricle choroid plexus.
journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
abstract: The choroid plexus (ChP) is a highly vascularized structure located in the brain ventricles that plays important roles in multiple central nervous system functions. ChP enlargement has been implicated in many neuropsychiatric conditions such as multiple sclerosis, depression, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer's disease. However, limitation in the accuracy of the current segmentation tools highlight the need for more reliable methods to quantify ChP volume in healthy and clinical human populations. The shape and size of the ChP vary drastically from person to person, and currently there are no large ChP datasets which allow comprehensive training of segmentation models. Here we introduce DataPlex, a collection of 700 structural MRI brain images where the lateral ventricle ChP has been manually labeled and checked by expert human raters. DataPlex is balanced and representative across a wide range of scanning parameters, demographics, and clinical profiles, and subject-level information will be available for each labeled image. DataPlex will be open source to support the creation of reliable segmentation tools for the human lateral ventricle ChP.

title: The implications of biotin supplementation on multiple sclerosis, hair loss conditions, and thyroid disorders.
abstract: Biotin, a water-soluble B-vitamin, is widely used as a dietary supplement for hair, skin, and nail health. High-dose biotin (≥ 300 mg/day) has also been studied as a treatment for progressive multiple sclerosis (MS), although the clinical benefit reported in an initial randomized trial was not confirmed in a larger phase 3 trial, and it is not an approved therapy for MS. However, increasing evidence suggests that biotin supplementation, even at over-the-counter doses of 5-20 mg/day, can interfere with thyroid function tests, leading to potential misdiagnoses of hyperthyroidism and autoimmune thyroid disease. This interference occurs in immunoassays reliant on streptavidin-biotin binding, causing falsely elevated free thyroid hormone levels (T3, T4) and falsely suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), with the extent of interference varying by assay and laboratory platform. In this narrative review of clinical studies and case reports, we found that patients with MS and hair loss pathology, such as alopecia areata (AA), conditions frequently coexisting with thyroid dysfunction, may be vulnerable to misinterpretation of thyroid lab results due to biotin supplementation. Several case reports illustrate patients with MS misdiagnosed with Graves' disease or hyperthyroidism while taking high-dose biotin, with laboratory values normalizing after temporary discontinuation. In AA, no such cases have been reported to date; however, over 40% of AA patients exhibit thyroid autoantibodies and many patients with hair loss use biotin, suggesting a potential, though not yet demonstrated, risk in this population. Given the increasing use of biotin, clinicians must be aware of its impact on laboratory assays and ask patients about biotin use before thyroid function testing. The discontinuation period needed to avoid interference is not uniform and depends on the dose, renal function, and assay used; 24-72 hours is often sufficient for over-the-counter doses, whereas longer intervals may be needed for high-dose therapy. Improved awareness can prevent unnecessary treatments and misdiagnoses in individuals with MS, AA, and other autoimmune conditions. This review integrates neurological and dermatological autoimmune overlap in the context of biotin interference and addresses an underexplored gap in the literature. Further research is needed to examine biotin interference across different laboratory methodologies and patient populations.

title: Glial Contributions to Pain in Neurodegenerative Disease Models: A Systematic Review of Microglial and Astrocytic Evidence.
Bilateral Internuclear Ophthalmoplegia Caused by Minor Head Injury: A Case Report.
abstract: Bilateral internuclear ophthalmoplegia (INO) is rare, with vascular disease and multiple sclerosis being the most common causes. We report an unusual case of isolated bilateral INO following minor brain injury. A 61-year-old Asian woman developed binocular diplopia after a minor motorbike accident. Neurological examination revealed bilateral INO with impaired adduction in both eyes and abducting nystagmus in the contralateral eye. Initial brain computed tomography was unremarkable, but brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) 2 days later revealed a subtle paramedian pontomesencephalic hyperintensity on T2-weighted imaging, which became more pronounced with contrast enhancement, suggesting the axonal injury secondary to trauma. Minor head trauma can cause bilateral INO due to subtle brainstem injury, even without other deficits. Shear forces may lead to vascular and axonal damage in the medial longitudinal fasciculus. MRI with contrast is essential for detection. Although rare, isolated bilateral INO should be considered posthead trauma.

title: Congenital Hypoplasia of the C1 Posterior Arch Masquerading as Multiple Sclerosis: A Case Report.
abstract: Hypoplasia of the C1 posterior arch is a rare congenital anomaly, classified using the Currarino system into subtypes A through E depending on the extent and nature of arch deficiency. The majority of cases are incidental radiological findings; symptomatic presentations causing cervical myelopathy are exceptionally uncommon and not well represented in the surgical literature. In such cases, the absence of established management guidelines renders clinical decision-making particularly challenging. We present a case of a 45-year-old male surgeon who presented with a one-year history of episodic bilateral upper and lower limb weakness. Initial investigations, including brain and cervical spine MRI, were interpreted as consistent with a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis, for which treatment was commenced. Following a symptom-free interval after a one-month course of corticosteroids, the patient experienced a recurrence at eight months, prompting dynamic MRI of the cervical spine, which revealed a type C hypoplastic C1 posterior arch causing dynamic spinal cord compression during hyperextension. The diagnosis was revised accordingly. Supplementary investigations confirmed atlantoaxial stability and normal vertebral artery anatomy bilaterally. The patient provided consent and underwent posterior surgical decompression of the entire posterior arch, without instrumented fusion. Intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring guided the extent of resection; decompression began on the fibrous left-sided arch, extending to the level of the vertebral artery groove, followed by the bony right-sided arch, sequenced to preserve facet joint integrity. The patient achieved complete symptom resolution postoperatively. This case highlights the diagnostic challenge posed by symptomatic C1 arch hypoplasia, which may mimic demyelinating disease, and demonstrates that surgical decompression, guided by intraoperative neurophysiological monitoring and tailored to arch morphology, can achieve excellent neurological outcomes without the need for instrumented stabilisation.

title: Coding Pregnancy: How Classification May Shape Clinical Research and Practice.
journal: Journal of evaluation in clinical practice
abstract: RATIONALE, AIMS, AND OBJECTIVES: The underrepresentation of pregnant people in clinical research limits the availability of reliable evidence for clinical practice. While this gap is often attributed to ethical and regulatory constraints, less attention has been paid to the role of medical classification systems in shaping the utility of Real-World Data (RWD). This paper examines how the coding of pregnancy within the International Classification of Diseases (ICD) and the Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities (MedDRA) may influence evidence generation and use. METHODS: We conducted a conceptual analysis of ICD and MedDRA, focusing on how pregnancy and related events are encoded. Drawing on literature from medical classification, pharmacovigilance, and evidence-based practice, we assess how classificatory fragmentation may affect data identification, retrieval and interpretation. An example from multiple sclerosis care is used for contextual illustration. RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: Pregnancy-related information is fragmented across different coding elements, without explicitly capturing the crucial temporal and clinical context. This structural limitation may hinder the reconstruction of pregnancy episodes, affecting the capacity of observational research to compensate for interventional research gaps. To overcome this, we propose a three-step approach: (1) providing dedicated training on the correct use and interpretation of existing classification systems; (2) complementing these infrastructures with a standardised minimum dataset to systematically link pregnancy variables; and (3) establishing a feedback loop from secondary research to continuously improve clinical documentation. Ultimately, this strategy can support robust RWD generation and more inclusive, evidence-based care.

title: Microbiome-Derived Metabolites in Multiple Sclerosis: Mechanisms of Immune Regulation and Therapeutic Potential: A Literature Review.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune neuroinflammatory disease characterized by immune dysregulation, demyelination, and neurodegeneration of the central nervous system (CNS). Increasing evidence suggests that gut microbiota and microbiome-derived metabolites play important roles in the pathogenesis and progression of MS by modulating the gut-brain-immune axis. This narrative review examines the possible immunomodulatory effects of microbiome-derived metabolites in MS, with particular emphasis on short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), tryptophan-derived metabolites, and polyamines, and evaluates their potential therapeutic implications. This review was conducted using the most recent available studies relevant to the topic. The search included PubMed, Google Scholar, and PMC databases. Eligible studies focused on randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, observational studies, reviews, and other publications that examined the role of microbiota and its metabolites in MS. The reviewed evidence indicates that MS-associated dysbiosis is accompanied by altered microbial metabolite production, disruption of regulatory T cell (Treg)/T helper 17 (Th17) balance, impaired barrier integrity, and increased neuroinflammation. SCFAs, tryptophan-derived metabolites, and polyamines demonstrate immunoregulatory effects through modulation of T-cell responses, cytokine signaling, and inflammatory pathways. Microbiota-targeted interventions, including probiotics, prebiotics, dietary modulation, and metabolite supplementation, have shown promising immunological and clinical effects. However, methodological heterogeneity, small cohorts, variable interventions, and insufficient long-term clinical validation limit definitive conclusions regarding therapeutic efficacy. Future large-scale longitudinal and multi-omics studies are crucial for clarifying the underlying mechanisms and unlocking microbiota-targeted strategies to manage MS more effectively.

title: Comorbidity Burden and Social Determinants of Health Among U.S. Hospitalizations for Multiple Sclerosis: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis.
abstract: Individuals hospitalized with Multiple Sclerosis (MS) often experience comorbid conditions that affect their quality of life and also face social determinants of health (SDOH) that affect outcomes. Data were leveraged from the 2019 National Inpatient Sample database, a component of the Nationwide Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project, a government survey of hospitalizations across the US, and theoretically representative of all hospitalizations in the US. We compared patients hospitalized with MS to patients hospitalized without MS across demographic characteristics and common concomitant diagnoses. In a secondary analysis restricted to MS hospitalizations, we examined the association of comorbidities and SDOH with length of stay. Between January 2019 and December 2019 there were a total of 25,155 hospitalizations for MS and 35,392,578 hospitalizations without MS. Mean age at admission was 45.9 years for MS versus 50.2 years for non-MS hospitalizations (p < 0.001). Patients hospitalized with MS were more likely to be female and more diverse than non-MS hospitalizations. Patients with MS were more likely to have a diagnosis of anxiety (18.9% versus 10.2%, p < 0.001), chronic pain (10.5% versus 5%, p < 0.001), and depression (21.8% versus 9.9%, p < 0.001) compared to non-MS hospitalizations. Among MS hospitalizations, depression diagnoses were reported less often among Black vs. non-Black (16.6% versus 23.6%, p < 0.001), Hispanic vs. Non-Hispanic (13.8% versus 22.7%, p < 0.001), and patients on Medicaid vs. non-Medicaid (19.1% versus 22.6%, p < 0.001). In a regression model restricted to MS patients, number of comorbidities and Black compared to non-Black race corresponded to increasing length of stay. MS patients have higher rates of anxiety, depression, and pain compared to non-MS patients. Minoritized groups with MS are less likely to be given a secondary diagnosis code for depression, anxiety or pain, possibly reflecting underdiagnosis of these conditions.

title: Investigation of astaxanthin-loaded hollow gold nanoparticles in mitigating the EAE mice model of multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a progressive neurological autoimmune disorder that affects the central nervous system. Current therapies lack the disease-modifying potential and precision. Astaxanthin is a naturally derived marine compound with potent biological properties and has been reported to mitigate the effects of multiple sclerosis. Herein, we aimed to develop astaxanthin-loaded gold nanoparticles to enhance precision in delivery to the brain by the efficient carrier properties of the gold nanoparticles. In this study, we employed an experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) mouse model of multiple sclerosis and treated for 3 weeks with free astaxanthin (6 mg/kg) and astaxanthin-loaded hollow gold nanoparticles (0.6 mg/kg), a 10-fold lower dose of the drug. The outcomes were evaluated by biochemical, pathological, histological, and hematological parameters. Our findings indicate that astaxanthin-loaded gold nanoparticles significantly improved the disease outcomes. Our findings suggest that astaxanthin-loaded hollow gold nanoparticles improved oxidative-stress indicators and motor deficits and imparted significant cellular protection in the disease condition. Overall, this study highlights the potential of astaxanthin-loaded hollow gold nanoparticles to improve neurological outcomes in the EAE mice model.

title: Effects of adjunctive craniosacral therapy to conventional physiotherapy on postural responses and autonomic function in individuals with multiple sclerosis: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: Craniosacral Therapy (CST) has emerged as a complementary approach in neurological rehabilitation, but its effects in multiple sclerosis (MS) remain unclear. To investigate the effects of adding CST to conventional physiotherapy on postural control and autonomic function in patients with MS. Thirty patients with relapsing-remitting MS were randomly assigned to a CST group ( Significant group × time interactions were found for Adaptation Test (toes-down) and Motor Control Test (back-small) latency measures, with greater reductions in response latency over time in the CST group (ADT toes-down: CST added to conventional physiotherapy may influence specific postural response parameters in patients with MS. However, no between-group superiority was demonstrated, and no significant treatment effect on autonomic function was observed. Further studies with larger samples are needed to confirm these findings.
