title: Evaluating healthcare professional-led physical activity promotion interventions for individuals with multiple sclerosis: a scoping review.
abstract: Identification and evaluation of the full range of components within complex interventions is critical to explaining their impact and informing clinical decision-making. Our aim is to identify physical activity promotion interventions suitable for implementation by healthcare professionals among individuals with multiple sclerosis, and to determine whether they meet current best-practice recommendations. We searched nine databases from inception up to May 2025. Articles were eligible if they included adults (≥18 years) with diagnosis of multiple sclerosis, evaluated interventions incorporating strategies to promote physical activity, reported outcomes of participation or its predictors, and identified healthcare professionals as deliverers. We identified 28 distinct interventions. Interventions showed limited alignment with existing recommendations regarding use of behavioural strategies, diversity of deliverers, theoretical underpinning, adherence to physical activity guidelines, range of activity options, and follow-up assessment. In contrast, alignment was stronger for duration and frequency of involvement, multimodal delivery, and inclusion of behaviour support components. While healthcare professional-led interventions represent a promising approach to promoting physical activity among individuals with multiple sclerosis, our component-level analysis reveals inconsistent alignment with best-practice recommendations, potentially undermining intervention impact. By clarifying where current interventions diverge from recommendations, we offer a framework to strengthen the design of future interventions.

title: Timing of high-efficacy therapy initiation in multiple sclerosis: a multicenter real-world analysis from Argentina.
abstract: Early initiation of high-efficacy therapies (HETs) in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS) is associated with improved long-term outcomes, yet real-world treatment trajectories may not reflect this paradigm. We aimed to quantify delays in diagnosis and treatment initiation in RRMS and assess whether these differ across first-line strategies in Argentina. We conducted a multicenter registry-based study including treatment-naïve RRMS patients from the Argentine Multiple Sclerosis Registry (RelevarEM). Three intervals were evaluated: symptom-to-diagnosis/treatment indication (T1), diagnosis/treatment indication-to-treatment initiation (T2), and symptom-to-treatment initiation (T3). Delays were compared across oral, injectable, and high-efficacy therapies using descriptive analyses and multivariable accelerated failure time models adjusted for demographic, clinical, and healthcare-related factors. A total of 389 patients were included. The interval from diagnosis/treatment indication to treatment initiation (T2) was comparatively similar across groups (approximately 1-2 months). In contrast, the symptom-to-treatment interval (T3) was longer among patients initiating HETs versus oral therapies (adjusted median 9.13 vs 2.58 months; +6.54 months), with the excess time concentrated predominantly before the recorded diagnosis/treatment-indication milestone. Sensitivity analyses suggested heterogeneity within HETs. These findings suggest that the longer time to HET initiation is primarily attributable to the interval preceding the recorded diagnosis/treatment-indication milestone, whereas the subsequent interval to treatment initiation was comparatively similar across treatment classes.

title: Objective assessment of gaze stabilization exercises in people with multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Dizziness and instability in gaze and posture are common symptoms in people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS). The vestibular ocular reflex (VOR) is one of the main functions of the vestibular system that may lead to gaze and postural instability if impaired. Therefore, it is important to understand if gaze stabilization is impaired in PwMS and recommend the appropriate management plan. To objectively compare the Vestibular Ocular Reflex exercise (VORx1) metrics including eye gaze compliance, head speed compliance, symptoms and tasks perceived difficulty rating scores between PwMS (with and without dizziness) and matched healthy controls using the VestAid software. Forty-three PwMS (21 with dizziness and 22 without dizziness) and 40 healthy controls participated in this study. A tablet app (VestAid) investigational software device was utilized to record the VORx1 metrics in horizontal trials. The VORx1 exercise is best described as the subject moving the head in the horizontal plane approximately 30° to the right and left from a target 90 cm in front of the persons face at the prescribed frequency (80 beats per minute) while keeping the non-moving target in focus. Subjects were exposed to 12 randomized visual scenes with static and optokinetic backgrounds. Gaze compliance, head speed compliance, symptoms rating, and the perceived difficulty were assessed after each visual scene. Results were analyzed using ANOVA, controlling for age, sex, and education level. Significant group effects were observed for the eye gaze compliance, head speed compliance, perceived difficulty scores, and symptoms rating. For the eye gaze compliance and head speed compliance, healthy controls performed better than PwMS. For perceived difficulty, healthy controls rated the tasks easier than dizzy PwMS. For symptom's rating, dizzy PwMS had more reports of headache, fogginess, and nausea than healthy controls. Considering all subjects together, we observed no significant effect of exercise condition on head compliance (p = 0.21). However, significant effect of exercise condition was found on task difficulty ratings (p < 0.001). Preliminary analyses suggest that PwMS with dizziness performed the worst with eye gaze compliance, head speed compliance, perceived task difficulty, and consistently experienced the most severe symptom scores. Additional studies are required to determine if the subjects optimized their gaze stability by slowing their speed of head turning while performing VOR exercises.

title: Optimizing myelin water imaging in multiple sclerosis.
abstract: Myelin water imaging (MWI) allows in vivo quantification of myelin content using MRI. Multi-echo gradient-echo (MEGRE) sequences with Variable Flip Angles (VFA), combined with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), can generate robust, whole-brain myelin water fraction (MWF) maps more efficiently than conventional implementations. We evaluated how spatial resolution and number of flip angles affect MWI quality in a clinical research setting. Fifteen people with MS and ten healthy controls were scanned at 3 T (Siemens VIDA). MRI included multi-shell DWI and 3D-MEGRE acquired at 2.0 mm and 2.5 mm isotropic resolution. Twelve echoes were acquired at five flip angles. MWF was quantified based on a three-compartment T1, T2*, and DWI model, and determined in normal appearing white matter (NAWM), lesions and corpus callosum. Associations between MWF across resolutions and VFA schemes were assessed using Bland-Altman, ICC-C and ICC-AA. MWF was highest in corpus callosum (10.2 ± 1.1%), intermediate in NAWM (7.9 ± 0.7%), and lowest in lesions (4.9 ± 0.7%) (values for 2.0 mm and FA5). A FA4 MEGRE protocol showed comparable MWF values, while FA3 systematically overestimated MWF and showed greater variability, particularly in lesions. ICC-C between spatial resolutions was good to excellent (0.80-0.91), ICC-AA was moderate to good (0.66-0.81), indicating that the two resolutions should not be treated interchangeably. QC monitoring of fitting results is recommended to strengthen reliability of MWF results. MWI duration can be shortened with a FA4 MEGRE protocol. Resolution choice should be guided by study aims, as 2.0 mm and 2.5 mm were not fully interchangeable.

title: Gray Matter Damage and Long-Term Disability, Cognitive Outcome, and Survival in Patients With Multiple Sclerosis.
Mesenchymal Stem Cell Therapy for Multiple Sclerosis: Harnessing Immunological Properties.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic inflammatory autoimmune disease triggered by damage to the central nervous system (CNS). This CNS damage is caused by the attack of autoreactive T cells against the myelin sheath. Genetic and environmental factors contribute to the development of MS, and the condition causes serious disabilities and exerts substantial health burdens. Although various disease-modifying agents have been developed, they have critical limitations; hence, effective interventions are required. In this context, cell transplantation therapy using mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs), hematopoietic stem cells, neural precursors, neural stem cells, and induced pluripotent stem cells is considered a feasible alternative therapeutic approach. MSCs are adult stem cells that differentiate into multiple lineages and exert immunomodulatory, neuroprotective, and neuroregenerative effects. Therefore, MSCs are considered a promising treatment option for MS owing to their ease of isolation and low immunogenicity. This review summarizes the potential therapeutic benefits of the latest MSC-based approaches for MS treatment in animal models and humans. Furthermore, the review discusses the immunological role of MSCs and future directions for their applications.

title: Mandatory national clinical audits as a tool to drive improvements in multiple sclerosis outcomes.
abstract: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a complex, time-critical neuroinflammatory condition where diagnostic delays and suboptimal treatment lead to irreversible disability. Despite an international consensus on best practices, equitable access to specialist care remains highly variable. We explore how implementing mandatory, continuous national clinical audit can potentially eradicate unwarranted clinical variation, drive systemic policy reform, secure targeted investment in specialist MS services, and create a positive feedback loop over time as services evolve. Drawing upon the highly successful models in stroke and cancer, we demonstrate how continuous, prospective data collection functions as an agent of change. We apply these mechanisms to MS care, using the internationally endorsed MS Brain Health: Time Matters policy recommendations, consensus quality standards, and their associated Quality Improvement tool as a blueprint for a potential mandatory national audit. Other recent initiatives, such as the Norwegian MS Registry, German implementation surveys and the UK MS Trust's Generating Evidence in MS Services (GEMSS) programme, provide proof of concept that standardised measurement improves operational efficiency, reduces non-elective emergency admissions, and generates robust health economic data necessary for strategic MS-related healthcare commissioning. To ensure equitable, cost-effective care and unlock funding for multidisciplinary teams, healthcare systems should be encouraged to invest in the infrastructure required for mandatory, continuous national audits of MS and other brain health conditions.

title: Impact of the Family-Centered Empowerment Model on Health-Promoting Lifestyle and Psychological Well-Being in Patients With Multiple Sclerosis: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic neurological disease that can affect patients' health-promoting lifestyle and psychological well-being and may also place substantial demands on family caregivers. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of a family-centered empowerment intervention based on the Family-Centered Empowerment Model (FCEM) on health-promoting lifestyle and psychological well-being among patients with MS, with the active involvement of their primary family caregivers. METHODS: This randomized controlled clinical trial was conducted from February to April 2025 at an MS clinic in Fars Province, southern Iran. It included 70 patient-caregiver dyads, comprising 70 patients with MS and their primary family caregivers. The dyads were randomly assigned to the intervention or control group, with 35 dyads in each group. Patients and caregivers in the intervention group took part in a structured family-centered empowerment program based on the four-stage FCEM. The program consisted of five to seven face-to-face educational sessions attended jointly by the patients and their primary family caregivers. The control group continued to receive routine care. Health-promoting lifestyle and psychological well-being were assessed at baseline, immediately after the intervention, and at the 2-month follow-up. RESULTS: At baseline, the two groups did not differ significantly in health-promoting lifestyle or psychological well-being (p > 0.05). Following the intervention, the mean health-promoting lifestyle score was 126.40 ± 25.18 in the intervention group and 102.62 ± 25.18 in the control group (p < 0.001). At the 2-month follow-up, the corresponding scores were 124.34 ± 22.39 and 104.22 ± 20.23, respectively (p < 0.001). A similar pattern was observed for psychological well-being. Immediately after the intervention, the mean score was 73.68 ± 13.83 in the intervention group, compared with 59.62 ± 10.24 in the control group (p < 0.001). At 2 months, the scores were 71.51 ± 12.82 and 61.34 ± 11.55, respectively (p < 0.001). Within the intervention group, scores increased significantly from baseline to both the post-intervention assessment and the 2-month follow-up (p < 0.001). Changes in the control group were comparatively small. CONCLUSION: A family-centered empowerment intervention based on the FCEM was associated with greater improvements in health-promoting lifestyle and psychological well-being among patients with MS compared with routine care. Involving primary family caregivers in MS education and self-management support may be a useful component of family-centered care. Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials: IRCT registration number: IRCT20190917044802N12. Registration date: 10/01/2025.

title: Neurodegenerative Diseases: Epidemiology, Risk Factors, Classification, Pathophysiology, Clinical Features, Diagnosis, and Therapeutic Strategies.
abstract: Neurodegenerative diseases are a growing cause of disability worldwide, particularly as populations age. Although these disorders differ in etiology and clinical presentation, advances in genetics, neuropathology, and biomarker research have identified shared disturbances in protein homeostasis, mitochondrial function, and immune regulation. These processes may contribute to selective neuronal vulnerability and neural circuit dysfunction. These findings are refining disease classification and diagnosis, yet effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited. Disease-specific abnormalities remain essential to clinical interpretation and treatment selection. Existing reviews often focus on individual disorders or isolated mechanisms, leaving the links between shared biology and disease-specific phenotypes insufficiently clear. We synthesize evidence on the epidemiology, risk factors, classification, and pathophysiology of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, Huntington's disease, frontotemporal dementia, Friedreich's ataxia, and multiple sclerosis. We compare their clinical manifestations and diagnostic approaches, including the evolving role of biomarkers, and critically assess established and emerging therapies. By distinguishing shared mechanisms from disease-specific abnormalities, we identify key translational gaps and explore how common biological disturbances may lead to distinct clinical trajectories. This cross-disease perspective may inform diagnostic reasoning, treatment development, and future comparative research.

title: Metabolomic Profiles Associated With Disease Severity in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Sensitive, minimally invasive biomarkers that reflect functional decline in multiple sclerosis (MS) are still lacking. Untargeted metabolomic profiling allows unbiased discovery of circulating biomarkers and dysregulated biological pathways underlying MS onset and progression. We aimed to identify candidate circulating metabolite signatures correlated with clinical, imaging, and patient-reported outcomes in MS and to characterize the underlying metabolic pathways. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of untargeted circulating metabolomic profiles from 541 samples of 323 people with multiple sclerosis (PwMS), including both relapsing-remitting and progressive forms, detecting 332 metabolites. Associations between metabolite levels and outcomes, including clinical disability (Expanded Disability Status Scale), functional tests (walking speed, manual dexterity, and processing speed), Neuro-QoL patient-reported domains, optical coherence tomography-derived retinal layer thicknesses, and MRI-derived measures, were assessed using linear mixed-effects models adjusted for age, sex, race, treatment status, and MS subtype. To identify clusters of metabolites jointly linked to outcomes, we applied Hierarchical All-Against-All Association Analysis and weighted correlation network analysis. Pathway enrichment was also performed using Fast Gene Set Enrichment Analysis on ranked effect sizes based on the RaMP database, excluding pathways with fewer than 3 metabolites. RESULTS: We identified multiple metabolites consistently associated with MS severity across clinical, patient-reported, and imaging domains. Metabolites such as p-cresol sulfate, p-cresol glucuronide, phenylacetylglutamine, and carnitine-derived species were linked to greater disease severity, whereas tryptophan betaine, ergothioneine, N-acetylcarnosine, and indolepropionate were associated with more favorable outcomes. Pathway analyses highlighted amino acid transport and metabolism, aromatic and branched-chain amino acid pathways, and solute carrier transporter systems, as well as bile acid, sphingolipid, and carnitine-related pathways linked to MS severity. DISCUSSION: Comprehensive integration of metabolomic, clinical, and imaging data in PwMS highlights distinct metabolites and metabolic pathways associated with MS severity. These candidate metabolites warrant external validation in independent cohorts and provide a rationale for future biomarker discovery studies aimed at improving disease monitoring and management in MS.

title: Clear Positive MOG Antibodies in Adults With Multiple Sclerosis Features: Diagnostic Challenges.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Distinguishing multiple sclerosis (MS) from myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) can be challenging because of some shared clinical and radiologic features. We aimed to describe adults with clear positive serum MOG antibodies (MOG-Abs) presenting with MS features and rethink their nosological framework. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective longitudinal study within the French NOMADMUS cohort and included adults from 2015 to 2025 tested clear positive for MOG-Ab in the serum with at least 1 MS-suggestive feature: (1) biological (CSF-specific oligoclonal bands [OCBs] and/or kappa free light chain index [KFLCi] ≥5.7) or (2) radiologic (≥1 lesion among juxtacortical lesion, Dawson finger, or inferior temporal lobe lesion). All MRI scans were reviewed blindly by an expert neuroradiologist. Minimum clinical and radiologic follow-up was 6 months. We classified patients as (1) typical MS when fulfilling 2024 McDonald criteria, with OCB and/or KFLCi ≥5.7 and showing no MOGAD supporting features, or (2) equivocal in all other situations. RESULTS: Among the 78 included patients (65% female, median age: 35 years), 23% were classified as typical MS and 77% as equivocal; all met MOGAD criteria, and 76% met 2024 McDonald criteria, without using central veinous sign or paramagnetic rim lesion, which have been rarely assessed. Myelitis followed by optic neuritis constituted the predominant clinical presentations in the whole cohort (45% and 32%, respectively) and in both groups. For typical MS cases, half of the patients did not receive maintenance therapy after the first MOG-Ab-positive event, 28% relapsed, 55% developed new silent lesions, and none showed lesion resolution (median follow-up: 1.9 years). For equivocal patients, 84% had OCB and 88% had ≥1 MOGAD supporting feature. After the first MOG-Ab-positive event, 72% initiated a maintenance therapy-mostly rituximab-15% relapsed, 46% developed silent new lesions, and 23% showed complete resolution of ≥1 lesion (median follow-up: 3 years). DISCUSSION: Clear positive MOG-Ab may occur in patients with genuine MS, and their presence may lead to therapeutic inertia. The substantial proportion of equivocal cases highlights current diagnostic limitations and underscores the need for longitudinal clinical and radiologic reassessment.

title: Long-Term Disease Control Following Completion of Cladribine Treatment in Multiple Sclerosis: Extended Follow-Up of the CladStop Cohort.
abstract: Long-term disease control after the standard two-year cladribine course in multiple sclerosis (MS) remains insufficiently characterized in real-world settings. We evaluated disease control, treatment re-initiation, and safety during extended follow-up of the multicenter CladStop cohort after treatment completion. We included 204 patients with relapsing MS who completed the approved two-year cladribine regimen and had ≥ 6 months of follow-up after treatment completion. Time zero ("CladStop") was defined as 24 months after first cladribine dosing. Co-primary endpoints were time to loss of no evidence of disease activity (NEDA-3) and annualized relapse rate (ARR) after CladStop. Kaplan-Meier analyses, multivariable Cox models, and mixed-effects Poisson regression were applied. Mean follow-up after CladStop was 44.2 ± 8.6 months. Overall, 81/204 patients (39.7%) lost NEDA-3. NEDA-3 survival was 82.8% (95% CI 77.8-88.2) at 12 months, 69.6% (95% CI 63.6-76.2) at 24 months, and 56.4% (95% CI 49.2-64.8) at 48 months. Forty-two patients (20.6%) relapsed, with an overall ARR of 0.06 (95% CI 0.04-0.08). Relapse rates decreased over time (rate ratio/year 0.74, 95% CI 0.55-0.999; p = 0.044). MRI activity occurred in 29.9% of patients and 6-month confirmed disability progression in 7.4%. A new DMT was initiated in 40.7% of patients. Relapses during treatment predicted earlier DMT initiation. Disease control remained durable in many patients after completion of cladribine treatment. However, over 40% initiated subsequent DMT during follow-up, indicating that prolonged treatment-free remission is not universal. Disease reactivation was driven mainly by inflammatory activity rather than disability worsening.

title: Safety of Multiple Sclerosis Treatments During Pregnancy: An Overview of the EU Regulatory Approach to Risk Management Planning.
abstract: Multiple Sclerosis (MS) may affect women of childbearing age. Information on safety of disease modifying treatment (DMT) in pregnancy is often limited at time of marketing authorisation. We summarised the EU regulatory experience with the implementation and performance of additional pharmacovigilance activities concerning safety in pregnancy and breastfeeding for medicines to treat MS. We reviewed EU risk management plans (RMPs) for centrally authorised MS DMTs to identify additional pharmacovigilance activities related to pregnancy and breastfeeding. Information was analysed descriptively for type of measure, data collection method and data source. For non-interventional cohort studies and follow-up of reported pregnancy cases, information on current status, planned and actual size and duration was retrieved. We identified 17 DMTs that included 21 additional pharmacovigilance activities related to pregnancy and breastfeeding across 15 RMPs. These comprised nine non-interventional cohort studies and four structured follow-up activities of pregnancy cases that had been started. Of those, three were terminated due to low recruitment with an inclusion rate slower than planned, while inclusion was faster than planned in three finalised activities. Inclusion rate was slowest in primary data collection and faster in secondary analyses and follow-up of reported pregnancy cases. Despite efforts to evaluate safety of MS medicines during pregnancy, recruitment and data collection remain challenging. Planning for use of multiple real-world data sources-including primary data collection, secondary use of electronic health records, and analyses of case reports-may help overcome these challenges and strengthen MS drug safety evaluations in pregnancy.

title: Digital Twins in Clinical Neurology: From Concept to Clinical Application in Multiple Sclerosis.
abstract: Patient digital twins (DT) are emerging as a promising paradigm for personalised and predictive healthcare. In neurology, and particularly in multiple sclerosis (MS), the availability of longitudinal, multimodal data provides a strong foundation for developing patient-specific digital models, including simulation-based and mechanistic approaches. However, it remains unclear to what extent current approaches represent integrated, clinically embedded DT systems. We conducted a narrative review to synthesise current concepts, modelling approaches and translational challenges of DT in neurology, using MS as an illustrative use case. Existing approaches were mapped to core DT components, including data integration, predictive modelling, dynamic updating and clinical integration. Current DT-related approaches in MS demonstrate substantial progress across complementary development tracks, including multimodal data integration, predictive modelling, digital biomarkers, mechanistic simulations, virtual-patient frameworks and in silico trials. These capabilities represent important building blocks of DT development but have not yet been fully integrated into continuously operating clinical systems. Core DT functionalities, including continuous bidirectional data exchange, real-time model updating and closed-loop interaction with clinical workflows, remain limited. Key challenges include data fragmentation, limited interoperability, lack of standardised validation, and regulatory, ethical and economic constraints. MS represents a highly suitable model domain for DT development. Future progress will depend on further maturing and validating individual modelling and data-integration capabilities, as well as on their integration into continuously updating, clinically embedded systems. Robust validation, scalable infrastructures and appropriate governance frameworks will be essential to establish safe, effective and clinically actionable use in practice.

title: Correction to "Italian Delphi Consensus on Maternity Care in Multiple Sclerosis: Toward an Interdisciplinary Model of Care".
The Impact of Cladribine Tablets on Cognition Over One Year in Patients With Multiple Sclerosis: A Preliminary Study.
abstract: Cognitive impairment is common in multiple sclerosis (MS), affecting >40% of patients. Cladribine tablets are a high-efficacy MS disease-modifying therapy to prevent relapses and limit disease progression. Our previous study showed cortical gray matter lesion stability over one year after the start of cladribine, though its effect on cognition is not well known. This study aimed to investigate the one-year impact of cladribine tablets on cognition in multiple sclerosis. Fourteen MS subjects [age (mean ± SD) 50.2 ± 10.8, 7.14% men, 57.1% relapsing-remitting MS (n = 8), 42.9% secondary progressive (n = 6), expanded disability status scale 4.1 ± 2.1] were administered the Brief Repeatable Battery of Neuropsychological Tests (BRB-N) and the Stroop Color and Word Test (Stroop) at an average of 1.5 months from cladribine start. The BRB-N measures information processing speed (Symbol Digit Modalities Test, Paced Auditory Serial Addition Test [PASAT]), verbal memory (Selective Reminding Test [SRT]), visual-spatial memory (10/36 Spatial Recall Test), and verbal fluency (Word List Generation). Stroop assesses processing speed and executive function. When available, alternate versions of the individual cognitive tests were used at follow-up to reduce practice effects. Paired t-tests compared within-subject baseline and follow-up data. After one year, no worsening was noted on any cognitive test. Furthermore, both PASAT 3-second total correct and SRT total delayed recall trended toward improved scores on-study, with an average 3.4 (p = 0.07) and 1.1 (p = 0.05) point increase, respectively. In this preliminary study, no clear decline in cognitive performance was detectable over one year in patients newly started on cladribine tablets.

title: L’utilizzo dei servizi sanitari in Italia da parte di persone con background migratorio: il caso della sclerosi multipla.
abstract: Healthcare service use among people with Multiple Sclerosis (MS) and a migration background (pwMSMB) in Italy remains poorly characterized. In the framework of IMPACT-MS project to compare sociodemographic, clinical, and healthcare-utilization profiles of pwMSMB by country-of-origin income level, using real-world data of MS register. Retrospective analysis (2000-2025) of the Italian MS Registrer (RISM), including 3,404 adults with confirmed MS and available residence data. Countries of origin were classified as high-income or lower-middle-income (World Bank Atlas 2025). Mixed-effects logistic regression (random intercept for center) compared groups on sociodemographic, clinical, and healthcare-utilization variables. 56% of pwMSMB originated from high-income countries, 44% from lower-middle-income countries. Lower-middle-income origin was associated with younger age (OR=0.93, p=0.004), lower likelihood of Southern Italy/Islands residence (OR=0.33, p<0.001), higher disability at first access (OR=1.16, p<0.001), and modestly greater diagnostic delay (OR=1.00, p=0.038). No significant differences emerged in treatment exposure or service-use frequency. Country-of-origin income was not associated with markedly different quantitative service access, but was linked to demographic, geographic, and clinical differences - particularly higher disability at intake - warranting further population-based research on unmet needs among pwMSMB. Key limitations include the lack of migration-status data, reliance on indirect proxies of service use that cannot capture socio-cultural barriers or care quality, register coverage limited to people already accessing MS centers, and the observational design, which precludes causal inference.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Neurology: A Critical Narrative Review of Clinical Evidence, Translation, and Responsible Implementation.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to neuroimaging, electrophysiology, clinical text, and digitally measured behavior, but reported performance often exceeds the maturity of clinical evidence. We conducted a structured narrative review, informed by SANRA principles, of English-language human studies, reviews, and regulatory sources identified in PubMed/MEDLINE and IEEE Xplore from January 2022 through July 2026; older landmark studies were retained when necessary for historical or methodological context. We applied a common translational-evidence framework across six prespecified neurological domains to distinguish technical performance from external validation, prospective clinical evaluation, implementation, and demonstrated patient benefit. Evidence was appraised according to cohort representativeness, patient-level data separation, external and prospective validation, calibration, clinical comparators, regulatory status, workflow integration, and patient-level benefit. Across stroke, dementia, Parkinson disease, epilepsy, multiple sclerosis, and neuro-oncology, the strongest evidence concerns narrowly defined imaging and signal-processing tasks. A cluster-randomized stroke study demonstrated shorter thrombectomy workflow time, and several externally validated models show improved portability. In contrast, many high-accuracy classification and segmentation studies remain retrospective, single-dataset, internally validated, and uncalibrated. Multimodal learning, foundation models, federated learning, and large language models broaden capability but introduce additional risks related to dataset shift, bias, opacity, privacy, and automation. Neuro-AI should be judged by its intended clinical task and evidence maturity rather than headline accuracy. Multicenter external validation, prospective workflow evaluation, calibration, subgroup reporting, human-factors testing, and post-deployment surveillance are prerequisites for safe and equitable clinical use.

title: Effectiveness, safety and therapeutic potential of medical cannabis across treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders: systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Medical cannabis has been suggested to have a therapeutic role in selected treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. We analyzed the available evidence to assess the effectiveness and safety of these interventions in treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. For this systematic review and meta-analysis, we searched Web of Science, Cochrane, Embase, EBSCO, and PubMed for studies published between January 1, 1970, and April 25, 2026. We considered studies examining any type or formulation of medical cannabis in treatment-resistant neuropsychiatric disorders. Primary outcomes were disorder-specific clinical improvement measures. Safety outcomes were adverse events, serious adverse events, and withdrawals due to adverse events. Evidence from studies was synthesized as equivalent odds ratios (eORs) for comparative outcomes and as pooled proportions for single-arm safety outcomes, via random-effects meta-analyses. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 for randomized trials, ROBINS-I for non-randomized studies, and structured quality assessment for case series and case reports, and certainty of evidence was assessed with GRADE. This study is registered with PROSPERO, CRD420251148868. 127 eligible studies were included, of which 32 studies involving 3645 participants contributed to meta-analysis. Meta-analysis showed improvement in drug-resistant epilepsy (eOR 0.50, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.34-0.72), refractory pain (eOR = 0.48, 95% CI = 0.30-0.78), and refractory multiple sclerosis spasticity (eOR = 0.22, 95% CI = 0.07-0.75). Evidence for psychiatric disorders was scarce. Small randomized trials reported improvement in PTSD-related nightmares and cannabis dependence after failed cessation. Uncontrolled studies reported improvements in hyperarousal, residual obsessive-compulsive symptoms, and refractory Tourette syndrome. Findings for treatment-resistant anxiety were inconsistent, and schizophrenia did not show a reliable therapeutic effect. Controlled analyses showed higher odds of any adverse events in drug-resistant epilepsy (eOR = 2.22, 95% CI = 1.52-3.23) and refractory multiple sclerosis (eOR = 1.89, 95% CI = 1.01-3.52), with higher odds of serious adverse events and withdrawals due to adverse events also observed in drug-resistant epilepsy. In single-arm and real-world studies, pooled proportions of any adverse events ranged from 15.5% in multiple sclerosis to 66.0% in Tourette syndrome, with substantial heterogeneity. Adjunctive pharmaceutical cannabidiol has the most consistent comparative evidence for reducing seizure frequency in selected drug-resistant epilepsy. Evidence for refractory pain and multiple sclerosis is heterogeneous and varies by clinical indication, cannabinoid formulation, and outcome definition. Evidence in treatment-resistant psychiatric disorders remains limited and is insufficient to support routine clinical recommendations. Further high-quality studies directly examining diagnosis-specific and formulation-specific effects, safety, and tolerability are needed.
